An arc marker path is read counter-clockwise from its first angle to its second (the validation requires the first to be the smaller), so its normal, the left of the tangent, points to the arc's centre. A rect path has no written order, so its orientation is not yours to choose: use between or of for an oriented flux through a closed curve. A segment or polyline runs as written.

docs.title: Limits of this version
docs.text:
• A contour with an elliptical segment is refused at validation (model.shape_not_offered): use disk, rect, polygon, union and difference.
  • 3D model documents and model documents on an imported mesh are refused with route.not_implemented.
  • A where filter on a straight edge is decided exactly (the segment is cut at the filter's bounds; an edge that only touches the box is not reported). On a curved edge it is decided by the edge's bounding box, and a curved edge whose box encloses the filter's box strictly in every coordinate is not reported as a partial match, so a curve that crosses such a box while another edge of the boundary is selected is not warned about. An empty selection still lists the candidates.
  • axmp.mesh raises route.not_implemented for a 3D document (at /symmetry), a document on an imported mesh (at /mesh/file) and a document with no geometry (at /regions; axmp mesh prints a note for the last).

docs.title: Shape optimization
docs.text:
In lumped-element experiments, changing a detector's dimensions changes its signal coupling, inductance and stored energy. In this guide we compute shape sensitivities and run a bounded search. A shape sensitivity measures the change in one of these quantities per change in a design parameter. axionMultiPhysics provides optimizers that use those derivatives to search for a local maximum of sensitivity or a local minimum of stored energy within chosen bounds.

For an objective \(J\), parameter \(p\), field unknowns \(y\) and residual \(R\), the discrete adjoint gives

\[ \frac{dJ}{dp} = \frac{\partial J}{\partial p} + \lambda\cdot\frac{\partial R}{\partial p}, \qquad S\lambda = -\frac{\partial J}{\partial y}. \]

Here \(S\) is the symmetric tangent operator and \(\lambda\) is the adjoint field. The mesh moves with the geometry while keeping its connectivity. The adjoint supports axisymmetric magnetoquasistatic designs with linear materials; 3D, full-wave results and RF loss budgets are not differentiated.

For a solenoid, x is the coax inner radius divided by the winding inner radius. With SciPy installed, we compute derivatives of the scan figure of merit to quantify its dependence on x:

import axionmultiphysics as axmp

design = axmp.template("solenoid")
result = design.solve()
s = result.sensitivities(params=["x"], objectives=["F"])
print(s["gradient"]["F"]["x"], s["relative"]["F"]["x"])

The first number is the derivative in SI units; the second is the fractional change in the objective per fractional change in x. These are derivatives on the current mesh: mesh convergence should be established before optimizing.

We now run a bounded search for a local minimum of the stored energy the solenoid needs to reach the scan requirement:

opt = axmp.optimize(design, objective="W_at_req:optimistic",
                  params={"x": (0.3, 0.8)}, max_iter=30)
print(opt["converged"], opt["message"])
print(opt["parameters"], opt["value"])

The value is in joules, after scaling the field to the selected scan requirement (the optimistic benchmark is an illustrative preset, and the default scan target an illustrative choice). axmp.objectives() lists the other objectives, among them the coupling ("F" with sense="max") and the peak fields at the requirement. converged and message describe the search termination; design contains the returned design document and history records the iterations. Field caps are only reported unless added as explicit constraints on sc_surface_at_req or B_peak_at_req; sharp superconductor corners should be rounded before optimizing a peak-field constraint.

For sensitivities involving nonlinear iron or changes to mesh connectivity, we pass method="fd_remesh" to result.sensitivities. The API reference lists arguments and return values.

docs.title: Particle transport (beta)
docs.text:
Charged particles through a design's solids and its solved magnetic field: muons through a tracker in a solenoid's bore, electrons showering in iron, geantinos counting an acceptance. Geant4 runs in axmp-transport, a separate program; the package drives it from Python with axionmultiphysics.particles, which plans a run into chunks of events, starts the program on them, merges the chunks in a fixed order and estimates the requested outputs with their statistical errors. The package's library, its Python module and the axmp command never link Geant4: they exchange files with axmp-transport, as they do with axmp-mesher and gmsh.

Beta

The job format, the output arrays, the driver's interface and the command line may change between minor versions. Every number is Monte Carlo with statistical errors only: the dependence on the physics list and the approximations of Geant4's models are not estimated. Statistical error is not the total error. Nothing here is validated against measured data; the validation page lists what is checked against closed forms and published formulas.

This product includes software developed by Members of the Geant4 Collaboration ( http://cern.ch/geant4 ).

docs.title: A first run
docs.text:
import axionmultiphysics as axmp
from axionmultiphysics import particles, solids

res = axmp.Design(doc).solve(workdir="runs/solenoid")
fm = res.export_field_map("runs/solenoid/fieldmap", tol=1e-4)          # docs/guides/field_maps.md
sol = solids.from_partition(partition, materials, region_materials)     # docs/guides/solids.md
r = particles.transport(axmp.Design(doc), res, solids=sol, field_map="runs/solenoid/fieldmap",
                        sources=[{"type": "gun", "particle": "mu+", "momentum_eV_c": 2e8,
                                  "at_m": [0, 0, 0], "direction": [1, 0, 0]}],
                        outputs={"trk": {"hits": {"in": ["layer_0", "layer_1"], "track": "primary"}},
                                 "E": {"deposit": {"in": "layer_0"}}, "Em": {"mean": {"of": "E"}}},
                        events=10000, workdir="runs/solenoid/muons", seed=1)
print(r["Em"])            # e.g. "1.234e3 +- 0.012e3 (10000 events)": a Measured, value and statistical error
hits = r.hits("trk")      # chunk, event, track, parent, pdg, region, x_m, p_eV_c, t_s, ekin_eV

particles.transport(design, results, ...) is the route from a solved design: its regions are the solids (passed as solids=: this version does not run the partition export for the call, which without solids= raises particle.partition_unavailable; the solids document that Design.export_gdml returns can be passed, a route that the validation does not cover yet), its field the map (exported from results into <workdir>/fieldmap when field_map is not given; every patch serves its record's regions). Everything else goes to particles.run, which is particles.plan + particles.execute + particles.merge on a work directory and works with any solids list and any fields:

r = particles.run("runs/w", solids=sol, fields=[{"type": "uniform", "B_T": [0, 0, 1.5]}],
                  sources=[...], outputs={...}, events=100000, chunk_events=1000, jobs=8, seed=7)
r = particles.extend("runs/w", events=200000)    # bitwise equal to a direct run of 200 000 events
r = particles.load("runs/w")                     # the merged result from disk, nothing run again

particles.capabilities() says what this installation has (never raises): the program (found, path, its --check document, ok), whether the mesher exports partitions for the API route (partition_export, false in this version for both geometries) and the event generator (none in this version).

docs.title: The driver: axionmultiphysics.particles
docs.text:
particles.plan(workdir, *, solids, sources, outputs, events, fields=(), seed=1, chunk_events=1000, jobs=1,
               physics_list="FTFP_BERT", production_cut_m=7e-4, integrator=None, outside="refuse",
               quantum_eV=1e-3, stop=None, threads=1, program=None) -> dict          # run.json's content
particles.execute(workdir, *, workers=1)
particles.merge(workdir, *, allow_failed_chunks=False) -> ParticleResults
particles.run(workdir, **plan_kwargs, workers=None, allow_failed_chunks=False) -> ParticleResults
particles.extend(workdir, *, events, workers=1, chunk_events=None, allow_failed_chunks=False) -> ParticleResults
particles.load(workdir) -> ParticleResults
particles.transport(design, results, *, sources, outputs, events, composition=None, solids=None, field_map=None,
                    map_tol=1e-4, track_volumes=None, workdir=None, **run_kwargs) -> ParticleResults
particles.resolve_materials(doc, *, program=None) -> dict

The module is pure Python (numpy, scipy); importing it imports nothing of Geant4. It finds the program as program=, else $AXMP_TRANSPORT, else axmp-transport next to axmp, else on PATH; without one, plan raises build.requires_program (build it with -DAXMP_BUILD_TRANSPORT=ON and set AXMP_TRANSPORT).

plan validates everything before it writes anything, and refuses with a named code (below): the event count (events is required: a run never defaults to a number of events), the seed (an integer in [0, 2^64), events.invalid otherwise: two seeds equal modulo 2^64 would be one run recorded as two), the source, the physics list, the outputs, the fields and their coverage of the solids, the integrator, a tally that could overflow, and the geometry (Geant4's overlap check, particle.geometry_overlap). A numeric argument of the wrong type or range (jobs, threads, workers, production_cut_m, quantum_eV, a seed that is not an integer) and a debug that is not an object raise a plain ValueError instead. It resolves the NIST compositions of the solids against Geant4's tables (resolve_materials, below), then writes the work directory:

<workdir>/run.json                the plan, updated by execute, merge and extend
<workdir>/exchange/solids.json    the resolved solids list both Geant4 routes read
<workdir>/exchange/job_<j>.json   one job file per block of chunks; exchange/commands.txt: their command lines
<workdir>/out/chunk_<k>/          the program's chunks; out/record_<j>.json
<workdir>/results.json, merged/   written by merge
<workdir>/logs/                   the program's output per process, with its exit status
<workdir>/.lock                   the workdir's lock

One driver per workdir. plan, execute, merge and extend (and run and transport) hold an exclusive lock on the workdir (fcntl.flock on <workdir>/.lock) while they work; another process that tries meanwhile is refused with events.workdir_busy and changes nothing (load only reads and takes no lock).

Field maps of a run. The job files name a map that lies inside the workdir (the one transport() exports into <workdir>/fieldmap) relative to it (../fieldmap), so a copied or moved workdir reads its own map; every other map by its real absolute path, so a workdir reached through a symbolic link finds it either way. run.json records each map's path relative to the workdir and the SHA-256 of its manifest (fields[i].manifest_sha256; the manifest lists every patch array's checksum). execute, extend and run compare it, where the job files point, before any program starts, and refuse a map that changed or vanished with events.field_map_changed, naming the map and changing nothing: an extension would otherwise mix two fields.

workdir must be new, empty, or hold a planned run (which is planned again: its chunks are removed; events.workdir_not_empty otherwise). The run is cut into ceil(events / chunk_events) chunks (the last one short when events is not a multiple), and the chunks into jobs contiguous blocks of near-equal length, one job file each (fewer when there are fewer chunks). threads is the --threads of every process.

execute starts the job files, workers processes at a time (run defaults workers to the number of job files). A process that fails (non-zero exit status) has its incomplete chunks run again once, in one new process; a chunk still incomplete is failed. A chunk counts as complete once its manifest exists (the program writes it last and then renames the chunk's directory); the merge checks every array against its checksum.

merge reads every planned chunk: it is complete when its manifest's chunk, chunk_seed and events are the plan's (otherwise the merge is refused, events.chunk_mismatch) and every array matches its SHA-256 (otherwise the chunk counts as missing). The merged sample is the longest complete prefix of chunks 0, 1, 2, ... (with allow_failed_chunks=True, every complete chunk). A prefix of a sequence of independent chunks is an unbiased sample whatever made the others fail, and it is what an extension continues. Fewer events than requested make a partial result: partial true, missing_chunks (the planned chunks not merged), warning events.partial. Events are merged in (chunk, event) order, so the result does not depend on jobs, workers or threads.

extend(workdir, events=N2) (N2 at least the events requested so far, events.invalid otherwise; the same chunk_events, events.chunk_events_mismatch otherwise) reuses every complete full chunk (its checksums checked), runs a short last chunk again in full and replaces it, runs the new chunks, and merges: the result equals, bit for bit, a direct run of N2 events (arrays, tallies and results.json, timings aside).

Stop rules. stop={"output": NAME, "rel_error": r} (NAME an aggregate output) merges the smallest prefix of K >= 20 chunks for which the output on chunks 0..K-1 has stat_error / |value| <= r, or the planned chunks. It is evaluated on prefixes of complete chunks in index order, so the result does not depend on the number of workers; chunks beyond K that completed are kept on disk as beyond_stop and not merged. execute evaluates the rule each time a job file's process exits, and then stops the others and starts no more: the rule saves compute only at the boundaries of job files. With the default jobs=1 every chunk runs; plan jobs well above workers (for example a few chunks per job file) when the rule is meant to end the run early. run.json's stop records reason (rel_error or events), chunks and events.

Command line.

python -m axionmultiphysics.particles {execute,merge,extend} WORKDIR [--workers N] [--allow-failed-chunks] [--events N]

prints one JSON document, {"status": "complete" | "partial", "events", "events_requested", "missing_chunks"}, and exits 0 when complete, with exit status 5 when partial, 1 when refused ({"error", "code"} on stdout), 2 for a usage error (a malformed command, --workers or --events that is not a positive integer, or --events given to execute or merge; nothing is changed). --allow-failed-chunks applies to the merge that execute, merge and extend end with (the Python execute only runs and takes no such option). A scheduler can run the commands of exchange/commands.txt itself (one per job file) and then merge.

docs.title: Sources
docs.text:
Exactly one source in this version, a gun:

{"type": "gun", "particle": "mu+", "momentum_eV_c": 1e9, "at_m": [0, 0, -0.5], "direction": [0, 0, 1],
 "spot_sigma_m": 0.001}
  • particle: a name of Geant4's particle table (axmp-transport --check lists it) or a PDG code; a name it lacks is refused with particle.unknown_particle, whose message lists candidates (muon -> mu-, mu+; electron -> e-; pion -> pi+, pi-, pi0; close spellings);
  • exactly one of energy_eV (kinetic) and momentum_eV_c, positive; a momentum is converted to kinetic energy with the mass of Geant4's particle table;
  • direction: a non-zero vector (normalised) or "isotropic" (uniform on the sphere; a point source);
  • spot_sigma_m (default 0): a Gaussian spot, sigma per transverse coordinate, in the plane through at_m perpendicular to direction;
  • at_m must lie in a region of the solids (their surfaces included): plan locates it in the solids list and refuses a point beyond the world or in the world or a void, where the primary would have no volume to start in or would leave the domain at once (particle.source_invalid). The program refuses a job file whose at_m lies outside the world (exit status 2, nothing written), and ends the process (status 4, with a message) if a spot draws a vertex beyond the world.

Every event draws first u0 = G4UniformRand() (recorded as first_flat), then, for an isotropic direction, u1, u2: cos(theta) = 1 - 2 u1, phi = 2 pi u2; for a spot, u1, u2: rho = sigma sqrt(-2 ln(1 - u1)), psi = 2 pi u2, the offset rho (cos(psi) e1 + sin(psi) e2) with e1 the unit vector of d x z (x when d is along z) and e2 = d x e1. Any other refusal of the source is particle.source_invalid.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
outputs is {name: spec} (names [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*), each spec with exactly one kind:

kind spec value per-event variable {"deposit": {"in": REGION or [REGIONS]}} the energy deposited per event, eV per-event variable {"hit": {"in": REGION, "of": "x" \| "y" \| "z" \| "r" \| "phi" \| "t" \| "E_kin", "track": "primary" \| "any"}} at the event's first hit in the region (default track: the primary); undefined (NaN) when there is none; m, rad, s, eV per-event variable {"primary": {"of": "x" \| "y" \| "z" \| "px" \| "py" \| "pz" \| "E_kin"}} the primary as generated; m, eV/c, eV aggregate {"mean": {"of": VAR, "where": W}}, {"std": ...}, {"quantile": {"of": VAR, "q": q, "where": W}} Measured aggregate {"fraction": {"where": W}}, {"count": {"where": W}} Measured (over all events) histogram {"histogram": {"of": VAR, "bins": n, "range": [lo, hi], "where": W}} r.histogram(name) tally {"tally": {"grid": G, "in": [REGIONS]}} r.tally(name) hits {"hits": {"in": [REGIONS], "track": "any" \| "primary", "particles": [NAMES], "max_per_event": n, "keep_events": m}} r.hits(name)
  • W (optional) is {VAR: {"gt" | "ge" | "lt" | "le": x, "defined": true | false}, ...} (all must hold) or {"any": [W, ...]}. An undefined value satisfies only {"defined": false}.
  • A grid G is {"type": "cylindrical", "r_m": [r0, r1], "z_m": [z0, z1], "bins": [nr, nz]} (full rings) or {"type": "cartesian", "x_m": [..], "y_m": [..], "z_m": [..], "bins": [nx, ny, nz]}. A step's deposit goes to the bin of the step's midpoint; a deposit outside the grid or outside in (default: every region) is not tallied.
  • A hit is one record per step that enters a volume of the listed regions (its pre-step point lies on the volume's boundary, and the track's previous step is longer than Geant4's surface tolerance, 1e-12 m), taken at that point: track and parent IDs, PDG code, region (index in the solids' regions), position, momentum, global time since the primary vertex, kinetic energy. At most max_per_event records per event (default 100; the rest are counted as dropped); with keep_events, only the first m events in (chunk, event) order keep records. At some interfaces Geant4 takes a zero-length step back and forth across a face; the step after it records nothing, so no point is recorded twice. An excursion into a neighbouring volume shallower than deltaChord (0.25 mm) is collapsed by Geant4 to such a step: its entry is recorded and its return is not (measured: 11 such pairs among 174 375 hits of 5000 protons crossing slabs of 1 T and 0.2 T at grazing angles, none at normal incidence). results.json gives records, dropped, events_with_records and events_without_records.
  • Anything else is refused with particle.output_invalid, naming the output.

docs.title: Results and estimators
docs.text:
r[name] -> Measured        # an aggregate; KeyError for other names
r.histogram(name)          # edges (numpy.linspace(lo, hi, bins + 1)), counts per [lo_i, hi_i), errors, underflow,
                           # overflow, undefined
r.tally(name)              # edges, edep_eV (mean deposit per event per bin), stat_error, q_dep_J_m3, volume_m3,
                           # events, quantum_eV, lo, hi (the exact 128-bit batch sums), batch_events
r.events(names=None)       # chunk, event and the per-event variables, numpy arrays in (chunk, event) order
r.hits(name)               # chunk, event, track, parent, pdg, region, x_m, p_eV_c, t_s, ekin_eV
r.record, r.outputs, r.n_events, r.events_requested, r.partial, r.missing_chunks, r.warnings, r.workdir

A Measured is a float carrying stat_error, error (the estimator), events, events_defined, units, mc (true), and upper_limit, cl, interval where they apply. Arithmetic on it returns a plain float, so an error is never carried along silently. It prints its value to the decimal place its error supports (the PDG rule: the three leading digits of the error decide two significant digits for 100-354, one for 355-949, and 950-999 round up to 1000 with two), as "0.9981 +- 0.0021 (2000 events)" or "(1.235 +- 0.031)e-7 (2000 events)".

output value statistical error (error) mean the mean of the selected defined values s / sqrt(n), s with ddof 1 (sem); none below n = 2 fraction k / N over all merged events the Clopper-Pearson interval at 68.27 % (interval) and half its width (clopper_pearson) count k sqrt(k) (poisson) zero counts 0 none: the exact one-sided 95 % limit, 1 - 0.05^(1/N) for a fraction, -ln 0.05 = 3.0 for a count (upper_limit, cl); printed "< 0.26 (95 % CL, 10 events)", never 0 +- 0 no merged event NaN none, and no limit (reason: no events), for every aggregate std, quantile, tallies on all merged events batch means (batch_means)

Batch means: chunk k belongs to batch k mod 20; v_b is the statistic on batch b's events (a tally: its bin sum times the quantum over the batch's events), w_b = n_b / N, and sigma^2 = B / (B - 1) sum w_b^2 (v_b - vbar)^2 with vbar = sum w_b v_b and B = 20. Below 20 merged chunks there is no such error (stat_error None, warning stat.too_few_chunks). The functions estimate_mean(values), estimate_fraction(k, n), estimate_count(k) and batch_means(values, weights) are the same estimators for your own arrays.

Tallies are exact. Every event's deposit in a bin is rounded to quantum_eV (default 1e-3 eV) and added as an integer, per chunk in 64 bits and per batch in 128 bits (two limbs, merged/tally_<name>_lo.npy unsigned and _hi.npy signed, exact value hi x 2^64 + lo): the sums do not depend on the order of the threads or the chunks, and none can wrap. A plan whose chunk could reach 2^63 quanta (chunk_events x (kinetic plus rest energy) / quantum_eV) is refused with particle.tally_overflow.

results.json (schema axionmultiphysics.particles-results/1) carries beta, mc (the sentence "Monte Carlo (beta): N events, seed S; statistical errors only; physics-list dependence not estimated"), seed, events, partial, missing_chunks and per output its record: aggregates {"value", "stat_error", "error", "events", "events_defined", "units", "mc": true, "beta": true} (plus interval, upper_limit, cl), histograms their arrays, tallies the file names of their batch arrays, hits their counts.

run.json (schema axionmultiphysics.particles-run/1) records beta, seed, stage and instance, chunk_events, events_requested, every chunk (index, seed, events, job, status: planned, complete, failed or beyond_stop, attempts, sha256 of its manifest), the program (path, versions, data sets, command lines), the physics list, production_cut_m, integrator (with stepper), quantum_eV, outside, fields (as given, map paths relative to the work directory, plus each map's tol and its patches' error records), sources, outputs, stop, materials_resolved, warnings, partial, missing_chunks and events. Outside the program's record and timing it holds no time, host or absolute path.

docs.title: Seeds
docs.text: One master seed (default 1, always recorded) gives every chunk its seed: chunk_seed(seed, k) = derive_seed(seed, "transport", "transport", k), where derive_seed(seed, *keys) starts from z = seed mod 2^64 and for each key sets z = mix(((z XOR h(key)) + 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15) mod 2^64), mix being SplitMix64's output function, h(int) the int mod 2^64 and h(str) the first 8 bytes (little-endian) of the SHA-256 of its UTF-8. It is injective in the last key, so the chunks of one run have distinct seeds. Every event of a chunk is seeded from (chunk seed, event index) as the program describes below (particles.event_words gives its four words).

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
fields is a list; each entry serves the regions it names (default: every region for an analytic field, the patch record's regions for a map patch):

entry field {"type": "uniform", "B_T": [bx, by, bz], "regions": [...]} Geant4's G4UniformMagField {"type": "current_loop", "radius_m": a, "current_A": I, "z_m": z0, "regions": [...]} a circular filament on the z axis in the plane z = z0, counter-clockwise seen from +z for I > 0 (closed form with complete elliptic integrals) {"type": "map", "path": dir, "patch": name, "regions": [...]} one patch of an axionmultiphysics.fieldmap/1 map (Field maps) {"type": "map", "path": dir} every patch of a map, each serving its record's regions; the map's zero_field_regions are field-free

A region served twice is refused (particle.field_ambiguous), an unknown region or a malformed entry with particle.field_invalid (also a write_map patch named without regions).

One field per volume. Every logical volume gets a field object and a field manager of its own, a field-free one where no field serves its region, so that no volume inherits its mother's field (Geant4 hands a mother's field manager to daughters that have none). Every field manager uses the same integrator: Geant4's templated Dormand-Prince 4(5) stepper with G4IntegrationDriver (G4ChordFinder's kTemplatedStepperType; recorded as "stepper": "G4TDormandPrince45+G4IntegrationDriver"), never the interpolation, B-field, FSAL or QSS drivers. A step near a boundary is integrated past it and the boundary is then located by re-integrating from the step's start, so only the field within about deltaIntersection of the boundary enters the trajectory. A patch is correct about one grid cell beyond its region (its margin), so delta_intersection_m must be at most 0.1 of the finest spacing of the attached patches (refused by the driver with particle.integrator_invalid, and by the program for any job file it is handed: exit status 2, nothing written). Measured on a field jump at a sphere (1 T inside, 0.2 T outside): per-volume patches correct to 1 um beyond the boundary give the exact piecewise circles to 2e-6 m; a field that is zero at once beyond the boundary, a single point-located field, the interpolation driver or a deltaIntersection of 0.1 mm give 2e-4 to 6e-3 m. That accuracy holds for a track that enters a volume deeper than about deltaChord (0.25 mm): Geant4 can miss a volume that a chord of the step enters by less, so a track that grazes the sphere (entering by 1e-7 to 5e-5 m) leaves it with errors of up to 2.5e-3 m (0.5 GeV/c) and 7.6e-3 m (0.1 GeV/c), equivalent to an error of at most deltaChord in its impact parameter; entries of 1 to 3 mm are exact to 7e-6 m and 5e-5 m. A track started within a micrometre of an interface and parallel to it is the same case.

integrator takes any of delta_chord_m (2.5e-4), delta_one_step_m (1e-5), delta_intersection_m (1e-6), epsilon_min (5e-5), epsilon_max (1e-3) and min_step_m (1e-5), Geant4's defaults; positive, with epsilon_min <= epsilon_max <= 1e-2. A delta_intersection_m above 0.1 of the thinnest tube of the solids warns particle.delta_intersection_not_small.

Outside the maps. At set-up the driver checks that each region served by a patch lies in the patch's box enlarged by its margin (kind 1: the solids' (r, z) extent; kind 3: the corners of the solids' bounding cylinder in the patch frame), and that, when fields is not empty, every region is served or field-free by a map's zero_field_regions; otherwise it refuses with particle.field_outside_map, naming the region and the patch. With outside="zero" the run proceeds instead: unserved regions are field-free, a field call outside a patch's box plus margin at a point inside the volume returns 0 and is counted (outside_calls), and the result warns particle.field_outside_map with the total count and each map's boundary_ratio. During the run, a stepper's trial point beyond a patch's box outside the volume (tens of mm beyond a volume whose face is the box face) takes the value of the box's nearest point and is not counted: such values do not enter the trajectory.

The domain. The world and the voids (solids without a region) end the transport's domain: a track that is in them leaves it, its kinetic energy added to the event's exit_eV. A track is in them when it leaves the world, or at the end of a step longer than the surface tolerance that started in the world or a void and whose first micrometre (at most half the step) lies in the world or a void by a locate of Geant4's navigator without history. A step that merely ends in the world is no exit: at an interface between two regions Geant4 can report the world (the mother of both) for one zero-length step and return the track on the next.

docs.title: Physics
docs.text: physics_list is one of FTFP_BERT (the default), FTFP_BERT_EMZ (Geant4's most precise electromagnetic option) and QGSP_BIC (particle.physics_list_unknown otherwise, naming them; a high-precision neutron list *_HP is refused with particle.physics_list_unavailable). production_cut_m (default 0.7 mm) is one production cut for all particles and regions. Geant4 kills particles that loop in a field without progress; their number and energy are recorded per event, and the result warns particle.looping_killed when their energy exceeds 1e-6 of the deposited energy. A track that Geant4's navigator abandons as stuck (not moving for 25 steps, GeomNav0003; seen for a track that snakes along an interface where the field reverses, which a solved map does not hold but adjacent uniform fields of opposite sign do) is ended where it stands instead of the event being aborted: the event and its chunk complete, the track's number and kinetic energy are recorded per event (abandoned_killed, abandoned_eV; not in exit_eV), and the result warns particle.track_abandoned.

docs.title: Materials: NIST compositions
docs.text: particles.resolve_materials(doc) returns the solids document with its NIST compositions resolved against the Geant4 the program is built with (axmp-transport --nist); the driver runs it before every run and records materials_resolved (per material as: nist or one_component, and NIST's data). A material whose block is exactly {"nist": X} at X's own density (within 1e-9) becomes the NIST material itself; any other keeps one component and takes X's mean excitation energy and state where the document gives none; a density more than 1 % from NIST's warns particle.density_differs_from_nist. The residual of the second case and the reasons are in Solids for particle transport.

docs.title: Codes
docs.text:
code kind raised for build.requires_program error axmp-transport is not found (or not executable). events.count_missing error No events: a run never defaults to a number of events. events.invalid error events or chunk_events not a positive integer; a seed outside [0, 2^64); an extension below the events requested so far; a work directory without a planned run. events.workdir_not_empty error plan into a directory that holds other files and no run.json. events.workdir_busy error plan, execute, merge or extend on a workdir whose lock another process holds (the command line: exit 1 and the code). events.chunk_events_mismatch error extend with a chunk_events other than the plan's. events.chunk_mismatch error A chunk whose manifest names another chunk, seed or number of events than the plan. events.partial warning Fewer events merged than requested (exit status 5 on the command line). stat.too_few_chunks warning Fewer than 20 merged chunks: std, quantile and tallies carry no statistical error. particle.unknown_particle error A particle Geant4's table lacks; the message lists candidates. particle.source_invalid error Not exactly one gun, an unknown key, both or neither of energy_eV and momentum_eV_c, a non-positive energy, a zero direction, a negative spot, a spot with an isotropic direction, a position outside every region of the solids. particle.output_invalid error An output (or a stop) that is not one of the forms above. particle.field_invalid error A malformed field, an unknown region, a map patch without regions, an outside other than refuse or zero. particle.field_ambiguous error A region served by two fields; transport() given both fields= and field_map=. particle.field_outside_map error, or warning with outside="zero" A region beyond its patch's box plus margin, or a region served by no field; with outside="zero", the count of calls outside the maps. particle.integrator_invalid error An unknown or non-positive integrator value, epsilon_min > epsilon_max or epsilon_max > 1e-2, a delta_intersection_m above 0.1 of the finest map spacing. particle.delta_intersection_not_small warning delta_intersection_m above 0.1 of the thinnest tube of the solids. particle.physics_list_unknown error A physics list other than the three offered. particle.physics_list_unavailable error A high-precision neutron list (*_HP): not offered in this version. particle.tally_overflow error A chunk whose tally could reach 2^63 quanta. particle.partition_unavailable error transport() without solids=: this version does not run the design's partition export for it (capabilities()["partition_export"] is false). particle.density_differs_from_nist warning A NIST composition more than 1 % from NIST's density. particle.looping_killed warning Looping tracks killed carrying more than 1e-6 of the deposited energy. particle.track_abandoned warning Tracks that Geant4's navigator abandoned as stuck (GeomNav0003) were ended; their number and energy are in the arrays abandoned_killed and abandoned_eV. events.field_map_changed error execute, extend or run on a workdir whose field map changed or vanished since the plan (its manifest's SHA-256).

The codes of the solids list (particle.partition_invalid, particle.geometry_overlap, ...) are in Solids for particle transport. Each error is an AxionMultiPhysicsError with code and hint, whose message names the offending item and ends with . Hint: ...; each warning a particles.ParticleWarning whose message starts with its code.

docs.title: Limits of this version
docs.text:
• One gun per run; no event generator yet.
  • The transport is validated with axisymmetric solids lists only. 3D lists (tessellated solids from Design.export_gdml of a 3D design) are built and checked by axmp-transport --geometry (volumes, masses, overlaps), but no transport through them is validated yet (the 3D dipole of the demonstration skips).
  • transport() needs solids=: it does not run the partition export itself (capabilities()["partition_export"]).
  • Statistical errors only; the physics-list dependence is not estimated (compare FTFP_BERT with QGSP_BIC or FTFP_BERT_EMZ by hand where it matters). No energy-balance check yet.
  • Reproducible bit for bit on one build, compiler and platform; another build agrees statistically only.

docs.title: The program axmp-transport
docs.text: axmp-transport reads a job file, transports events, and writes NPY arrays and a run record. Its modes: transport (the driver's), probe (the fields at given points) and hello (muons through a silicon slab: a check of the toolchain). axmp-transport --geometry solids.json builds a solids list in Geant4 and checks it for overlaps (see Solids for particle transport); axmp-transport --nist NAME [NAME ...] prints Geant4's own data of NIST materials.

docs.title: Licences
docs.text: The source of axmp-transport is BSD-3-Clause. The running program links Geant4 (Geant4 Software License) and the LGPL-3 CLHEP that every Geant4 build contains. For that reason it is a separate program, it is built only on request (-DAXMP_BUILD_TRANSPORT=ON, off by default and always off when building a wheel), and no wheel contains Geant4 or CLHEP code. Geant4's data sets are distributed by CERN and are never redistributed or downloaded by this package. The full rule is in Installation: licensing of each wheel.

docs.title: Building it
docs.text:
You need a Geant4 from 11.2 up to, not including, 11.5, built multithreaded (GEANT4_BUILD_MULTITHREADED=ON), with its data sets installed (Geant4's GEANT4_INSTALL_DATA=ON, or an existing installation). The 12 data sets that Geant4 11.4 installs by default are 1.65 GB compressed and about 2.2 GB unpacked; Geant4 finds them under <prefix>/share/Geant4/data, or where GEANT4_DATA_DIR or the variable of a data set points. 11.4.3 is the version the project is tested with; another version in the range is accepted and reported as untested by --check.

cmake -S . -B build -DAXMP_BUILD_TRANSPORT=ON -DGeant4_DIR=<geant4 prefix>/lib64/cmake/Geant4
cmake --build build --target axmp-transport

The configure refuses a Geant4 outside the range or without multithreading and says what to change. (Geant4's own version file checks only the lower end of the range that find_package asks for, so the upper end is checked explicitly.)

docs.title: Checking an installation
docs.text:
axmp-transport --check

prints one JSON document on stdout (Geant4's banner and messages go to stderr): the program and Geant4 versions, whether that Geant4 is the tested one, the physics lists and modes offered, and the Geant4 data sets with where each was found, whether it is ok or missing, and whether the offered physics list requires it (FTFP_BERT reads G4EMLOW, G4PARTICLEXS, PhotonEvaporation and G4ENSDFSTATE). ok is true when every required data set is present. "geometry": true says that the program has the geometry mode, "nist": true that it has --nist; modes lists hello, transport and probe, physics_lists the three offered, stepper the pinned integration driver, and particles Geant4's particle table once FTFP_BERT has built it (name: PDG code, mass in eV, charge; ions left out).

axmp-transport --nist G4_WATER G4_SODIUM_IODIDE

prints {"schema": "axionmultiphysics.transport-nist/1", "materials": {NAME: {"density_kg_m3", "mean_excitation_eV", "state", "T_K", "pressure_Pa", "elements": {symbol: mass fraction}}}}, each value converted once from Geant4's units and written so that it reads back as the same double; a name Geant4's NIST manager does not know ends it with exit status 2 (named on stderr, nothing on stdout).

docs.title: Running a job
docs.text:
axmp-transport [--threads N] job.json

The run manager is always Geant4's tasking run manager with N threads (default 1), also for N = 1. Relative paths in the job resolve against the directory of the job file. Unknown or missing keys, wrong types and values out of range are refused before Geant4 starts, and so is a delta_intersection_m above 0.1 of the finest spacing of the map patches the job attaches (exit status 2, nothing written). A job file of the mode transport (schema axionmultiphysics.transport-job/1), as the driver writes it:

{"schema": "axionmultiphysics.transport-job/1", "mode": "transport", "out": "../out", "record": "../out/record_0.json",
 "chunks": [{"index": 0, "seed": 1234, "events": 1000}],
 "physics_list": "FTFP_BERT", "production_cut_m": 0.0007,
 "solids": "solids.json",
 "fields": [{"type": "map", "path": "/data/run1/fieldmap", "patch": "air", "regions": ["air"]}],
 "outside": "refuse",
 "integrator": {"delta_chord_m": 0.00025, "delta_one_step_m": 1e-05, "delta_intersection_m": 1e-06,
                "epsilon_min": 5e-05, "epsilon_max": 0.001, "min_step_m": 1e-05},
 "source": {"type": "gun", "particle": "mu+", "momentum_eV_c": 1e9, "at_m": [0, 0, 0], "direction": [0, 0, 1],
            "spot_sigma_m": 0.0},
 "quantum_eV": 0.001,
 "tallies": [{"name": "q", "grid": {"type": "cylindrical", "r_m": [0, 0.5], "z_m": [-1, 1], "bins": [10, 20]},
              "regions": ["iron"]}],
 "hits": [{"name": "tracker", "regions": ["layer_0", "layer_1"], "track": "any", "particles": null,
           "max_per_event": 100}]}

chunks is a list of {index, seed, events} run in the listed order in one process (the geometry and the physics are built once), one BeamOn each; seed is an integer in [0, 2^64). Every region is named explicitly (the driver resolves the defaults). fields, tallies and hits may be empty. debug is for tests only (fail_chunks: the process ends with status 4 on reaching one of these chunks, before running it).

Mode probe. {"schema", "mode": "probe", "out", "solids", "fields", "outside", "probe": {"points": "points.npy"}} with an (n, 3) float64 array of points in m: each point is located in its volume (a navigator of the built geometry) and that volume's field object is evaluated as the stepper would. It writes <out>/probe/B_T.npy ((n, 3), tesla), <out>/probe/region.npy ((n,) int32, the index in the solids' regions, -1 for the world and the voids, whose field is 0) and <out>/probe/manifest.json (outside_calls). Map patches are evaluated as FieldMap.evaluate evaluates them (bilinear in (r, z) for kind 1 with B_x = B_r cos(phi) - B_phi sin(phi), B_y = B_r sin(phi) + B_phi cos(phi); trilinear for kind 3 in the patch frame, rotated back; clamped within the margin), within 1e-12 of the field's scale. A point beyond its patch's box plus margin ends the probe with exit status 4 and fieldmap.outside_map on stderr (outside: "refuse") or gets 0 and is counted ("zero").

Mode hello. Muons through a silicon slab in an optional uniform field: a check of the toolchain, the seeding and the reproducibility.

{"schema": "axionmultiphysics.transport-job/1", "mode": "hello", "out": "out",
 "chunks": [{"index": 0, "seed": 1, "events": 200}],
 "hello": {"particle": "mu-", "energy_eV": [5.0e8, 1.5e9], "field_T": [0.0, 1.0, 0.0], "target_thickness_m": 0.01}}

A world box of half-lengths 1 m of G4_Galactic; a box of half-lengths 0.5 m by 0.5 m by half the thickness of G4_Si at the origin. The gun starts at (0, 0, -0.5 m) along +z with kinetic energy low + (high - low) u, u being the first random number of the event. A non-zero field_T attaches a uniform field to the whole world. Its arrays are event, seed_words, first_flat, ekin_eV, edep_eV (in the target), n_steps, n_tracks and field_calls.

Exit status. 0 success. 2 usage or invalid job. 3 refused at set-up: a required data set is missing, Geant4 is not multithreaded, SeedOncePerCommunication is not 0, or Geant4 does not build the pinned integration driver. 4 failure during the run: any Geant4 exception that is not a warning, including one that would abort a single event, ends the process with this status and writes no output for the chunk in progress (events are never dropped); so does a field call outside a map at a point inside its volume with outside: "refuse" (fieldmap.outside_map). An error is one line on stderr that starts with axmp-transport: error:. Nothing is written under out when the status is 2 or 3.

docs.title: Chunk outputs
docs.text:
For every chunk k, <out>/chunk_<k>/ holds one NPY file per array and manifest.json; the directory is written as chunk_<k>.<pid>.tmp (a directory of the writing process's own, so that a program left running by a killed driver cannot collide with a new one) and renamed when complete, replacing an earlier chunk_<k> (a chunk that did not finish is never renamed). Row i of every per-event array is event i of the chunk, whatever order the threads finished in. Mode transport:

array dtype, shape content event <u8 (n,) event index seed_words <u4 (n, 4) the four words that seeded the event first_flat <f8 (n,) u0, the first random number of the event primary <f8 (n, 7) x, y, z [m], px, py, pz [eV/c], E_kin [eV] of the primary as generated edep_eV <f8 (n, R) energy deposited per region (R regions, the solids' regions order) exit_eV <f8 (n,) kinetic energy of tracks entering the world or a void n_steps, n_tracks, field_calls, outside_calls, looping_killed <u8 (n,) per event looping_eV <f8 (n,) kinetic energy of the looping tracks killed abandoned_killed <u8 (n,) tracks Geant4's navigator abandoned as stuck (GeomNav0003), ended by the program abandoned_eV <f8 (n,) their kinetic energy (booked here, not in exit_eV) hits_<name>_count, hits_<name>_dropped <u4 (n,) records kept and dropped per event hits_<name>_event <u8 (m,) the hit records, sorted by event, then in the event's step order hits_<name>_track, _parent, _pdg, _region <i4 (m,) hits_<name>_x_m, hits_<name>_p_eV_c <f8 (m, 3) the pre-step point's position; momentum hits_<name>_t_s, hits_<name>_ekin_eV <f8 (m,) global time since the primary vertex; kinetic energy tally_<name> <i8 (grid bins) sum over the chunk's events of each event's bin total rounded to the quantum

manifest.json (schema axionmultiphysics.transport/1) records chunk, chunk_seed, events, threads, the versions, physics_list, production_cut_m, integrator (with stepper), quantum_eV, outside, regions, arrays (each array's file, dtype, shape and SHA-256), counters (field_calls, outside_calls, looping_killed, looping_eV, abandoned_killed, abandoned_eV, hits_dropped) and timing. The record (record, default <out>/record.json) records the status, the mode, the threads, the chunks run, seed_once_per_communication (always 0), the totals of field calls, outside calls, looping tracks killed and abandoned tracks, and timing: startup_s, the time from the start of the process to the first event (Geant4's initialisation, physics tables and thread start; about 1 s for FTFP_BERT on the cluster's nodes, whatever the number of threads), and total_s.

docs.title: Seeding and reproducibility
docs.text:
The seed of an event depends only on the chunk seed and the event's index in the chunk. The four 32-bit words are the outputs 2e and 2e+1 of the SplitMix64 sequence that starts at the chunk seed (the outputs of the generator of Steele, Lea and Flood, 2014), low half first. They are installed with G4Random::setTheSeeds(words, 4) as the first statement of the primary generator's GeneratePrimaries, on a MixMax engine, in every mode. Geant4 seeds the event itself first; the words overwrite that, so the chunk size is not limited by Geant4's refill of its seeds after 10 000 events. The program refuses to start when Geant4's SeedOncePerCommunication is not 0, the mode in which the seeds of events would depend on the thread that ran them.

An event is therefore the same whatever --threads is, whichever chunks ran before it in the process, and whichever position it has in a longer chunk with the same seed: the arrays of a chunk are bitwise identical in all those runs (the manifests differ in threads and timing only). This holds for one build, compiler and platform; another build agrees statistically only.

docs.title: Readout and multi-band scans
docs.text: In lumped-element experiments, a readout circuit turns axion-induced pickup flux into a current measured by a SQUID. A capacitor tunes the pickup and input coil to resonance. The circuit combines thermal noise from resistive elements with the amplifier's measurement noise and backaction on the coil. In this guide we compute readout noise and plan multi-band scans.

docs.title: From pickup flux to readout noise
docs.text:
The signal transfer and noise referred to the pickup's electromotive force are

\[ H_s(\omega)\equiv\frac{\Phi_{\rm SQ}}{\mathcal E_{\rm pickup}}, \qquad N_V(\omega)\equiv\frac{S_\Phi^{\rm tot}(\omega)}{\lvert H_s(\omega)\rvert^2}. \]

Here \(\Phi_{\rm SQ}\) is the SQUID flux and \(S_\Phi^{\rm tot}\) its total noise power spectral density (PSD). \(H_s\) has units of \(\mathrm{Wb/V}\) and \(N_V\) of \(\mathrm{V^2\,s}\). These PSDs are half the usual one-sided per-Hz PSDs.

With NumPy and SciPy installed, we tune to 1 MHz. Q sets the pickup loss; the default amplifier has uncorrelated noise and is matched for scan rate. We compute the effective circuit parameters and input-referred noise to characterize the readout.

from math import pi
from axionmultiphysics.circuit import series_readout

f0 = 1e6
readout = series_readout(
    L_p_H=1e-6, L_in_H=1e-7, f_Hz=f0,
    Q=1e6, T_K=0.03, M_H=1e-9,
)
eq = readout.equivalent(f_Hz=f0)
print(eq["L_eff_H"], eq["Q_loaded"], eq["T_eff_K"])
print(readout.noise_psd(2 * pi * f0)["N_V_V2_s"])

The first line gives whole-loop inductance in henries, loaded quality factor, and effective noise temperature in kelvin; the second gives input-referred noise. We use whole-loop quantities for scan reach: input-coil and lead inductances contribute even though they collect no signal. The model neglects SQUID input impedance; the resonance reduction applies locally around an isolated pole.

docs.title: Tuning across several bands
docs.text:
The multi-band and multipole scans (axionmultiphysics.multipole) are beta.

When a detector's size approaches an electromagnetic wavelength, its impedance can contain several resonances. A multi-band scan distributes time among tunable frequency intervals. In the engineering convention \(Z=R+iX\), positive \(X\) is inductive; a series capacitor or inductor cancels the source reactance:

\[ C=\frac{1}{\omega X}\quad(X>0),\qquad L_t=-\frac{X}{\omega}\quad(X<0). \]

The effective inductance is half the slope of the total tuned reactance with respect to angular frequency, including the tuning element.

We start with an ideal 100 nH pickup and an illustrative coupling of \(10^{-6}\,\mathrm{H\,T\,m^2}\). The same axionMultiPhysics calls accept sampled full-wave responses. We tabulate the pickup response and plan a multi-band scan to find the time required for the target reach.

import numpy as np
from axionmultiphysics import multipole

f = np.linspace(10e6, 150e6, 501)
omega = 2 * np.pi * f
table = multipole.source_table(
    f, 1j * omega * 100e-9, omega * 1e-6,
    convention="exp(+jwt)", source_unit="kappa_SI",
)
plan = multipole.multiband_scan(
    table, Q=1e5, live_time_yr=1.0,
    g_target=lambda f: np.full_like(f, 1e-15), rho_GeV_cm3=0.3, Q_a=6.8e5,
)
print(plan["bands"])
print(plan["t_req_s"])

The voltage column is the open-circuit amplitude per unit SI axion source coefficient, identified by source_unit="kappa_SI". For COMSOL data, we specify source normalization and any port load. axionMultiPhysics impedance data use convention="exp(-iwt)". Here Q specifies total resonator quality factor; alternatively, Q_mqs adds intrinsic loss to the table's resistance.

bands lists intervals in Hz and their tuning-element type. Defaults allow 30–300 pF capacitors and 10–500 nH inductors, removing 2.5 MHz at each band edge. t_req_s is the time to reach \(10^{-15}\,\mathrm{GeV^{-1}}\) across accepted bands; g_target_allocation_GeV gives reach after rescaling to the requested live time.

docs.title: Exporting port parameters to circuit tools
docs.text:
A full-wave sweep's port impedances can be written as a Touchstone file and simulated with an external circuit tool (SPICE, ADS, Microwave Office, scikit-rf). The engine's \(e^{-i\omega t}\) impedances are complex-conjugated into the \(e^{+j\omega t}\) convention these tools assume, so an inductor reads \(Z=+j\omega L\):

res = design.solve()                                   # a design with a fullwave section
report = res.write_touchstone("pickup.s2p", kind="S", z0=50)   # the solved rows
res.write_touchstone("pickup_dense.s2p", dense=True)   # an adaptive sweep's dense model curve (beta)
print(report["sigma_max"], report["passivity_violations_Hz"], report["reciprocity_error"])

From the command line, run axmp export-touchstone runs/NAME/results.json --kind S --z0 50 [--dense]. It exits with 0 when the file was written and is passive, 3 when it was written but is not passive, and 2 on an error. The file is Touchstone v1 with option line # Hz S RI R 50, increasing frequencies and a comment giving the port order and polarity (port 1 is the pickup).

The report gives \(\sigma_{\max}(S)\), which must not exceed 1 for a passive structure. A violation is reported as a warning and the data are written as computed, never clipped. The report also gives the asymmetry of \(Z\), which for a reciprocal design is zero to solver precision (about \(10^{-11}\)).

The perturbative conductor surface loss is not part of \(Z\). surface_losses=True adds its resistive part to the solved rows, but not the surface reactance. axionmultiphysics.touchstone.read_touchstone reads files back. Per-port reference impedances are written for S-parameters only, as a Touchstone v1.1 option line. Z and Y do not depend on z0: export them with one z0, or compute per-port S with z_to_s. Details are in S-, Y- and Z-parameters and Touchstone files.

multiband_scan uses local poles. axionMultiPhysics provides scan.finite_band to combine responses across resonances at each fixed tuning with a frequency-dependent readout within a capacitor-tunable interval. Further reading: dc SQUID readout chains (beta) or the API reference.

docs.title: Solids for particle transport (beta)
docs.text:
Geant4 transports particles through a tree of solids, each placed in its mother. axionmultiphysics.solids builds that tree from the mesher's description of an axisymmetric partition (the regions as disjoint faces in the (r, z) half-plane, bounded by curves whose exact parameters the mesher states) or of a 3D partition (the volumes of a 3D design, bounded by triangulated faces). It writes the tree as solids.json (schema axionmultiphysics.solids/1), which axmp-transport instantiates, or as GDML for any Geant4 application. Per region it reports the volume and the mass of the exact solid of revolution and of the solids that represent it. Nothing here needs gmsh or Geant4.

Beta

The module, the format of solids.json and the codes may change between minor versions. The partition comes from a hand-built table, from the mesher's info file of a bounded axisymmetric mode, or from an axisymmetric or 3D electromagnetic design (Design.export_gdml, 3D designs); the route from a model document to the partition comes later.

from axionmultiphysics import solids

doc = solids.from_partition(partition, materials, region_materials)   # chord_tol_m=None
solids.write(doc, "solids.json")
solids.write_gdml(doc, "design.gdml")
  • partition: the mesher's info file of a bounded axisymmetric mode, or the file of axmp-mesher --export-regions (a JSON object), with the extended entity table described below; for a 3D design, the file of --export-regions on its 3D mesher input (3D designs).
  • materials: the document's materials, {name: {"density": kg/m3, "particle": {...}}}. Other keys of a material (its electromagnetic or thermal properties) are ignored.
  • region_materials: {region: material name} for every region that has a face.
  • chord_tol_m: the chord tolerance of every region, in m; by default each region has its own (below). A 3D partition takes none (ValueError): its triangulation is the mesher's, made to the chord_tol_m given to the export.

solids.default_chord_tol(size_m) is min(1 µm, 1e-5 × size); solids.VOLUME_WARN is 1e-4; solids.SCHEMA is "axionmultiphysics.solids/1". Errors are AxionMultiPhysicsError with a code and a hint; the volume warning is a solids.SolidsWarning.

docs.title: The partition
docs.text:
The conversion reads, from the info file:

  • geometry: "axisymmetric" (a planar partition is refused with particle.planar_not_offered);
  • regions: {name: {"attr": ...}}; the regions are reported in the order of attr;
  • entities: the curves, each with tag, type (line, circle or ellipse), side ([the region on the left of the curve's direction, the region on its right], "exterior" outside the domain), and the extension below;
  • faces: [{"tag", "region", "loops": [[signed tags], ...]}], every final face of the partition with its outer loop first. A loop keeps its face on its left (the outer loop counter-clockwise in (r, z), the inner loops clockwise); a positive tag runs the entity from start to end, a negative one from end to start.

Each entity carries start and end ([r, z, 0], in m): the coordinates of its end vertices, start first along the curve. Entities that meet share the coordinates of their common vertex bit for bit, a point on the axis has r exactly 0, and a closed curve has start == end. An arc (circle or ellipse) also has center, radii ([a, b], a ≥ b; equal for a circle, also for the circular arcs that gmsh reports as ellipses), major_axis (the unit vector of the semi-axis a) and ccw (true when the curve turns counter-clockwise from start to end): the curve is c + a cos t u + b sin t v, with v the major axis turned by +90°.

Every other key of the info file (the regions' measures, the atoms, the boundaries, the timings) is ignored, and the output depends only on the geometry: not on the order of the entities, faces or inner loops, the tags, or where a loop starts. A table that does not describe closed faces is refused with particle.partition_invalid: no faces; a face that names an entity or a region the table does not have; an entity type other than line, circle or ellipse (an imported mesh has no exact curves); a missing start or end; a loop that does not close (consecutive curves must share their vertex bit for bit); a face that runs a curve with its region on the wrong side; an outer loop that is not counter-clockwise.

docs.title: Electromagnetic designs
docs.text:
Design.export_gdml(path, composition, *, solids=None, chord_tol_m=None, workdir=None, mesher=None) (beta) writes the GDML of an axisymmetric electromagnetic design, and returns the solids document:

import axionmultiphysics as axmp

design = axmp.template("core")
composition = {"winding": {"nist": "G4_Cu", "density": 8960.0}, "nb": {"nist": "G4_Nb"},
               "vacuum": {"nist": "G4_Galactic", "density": 1e-22}, "air": {"nist": "G4_AIR", "density": 1.205}}
doc = design.export_gdml("core.gdml", composition, solids="solids.json")

The route is the design's mesher input (the one axmp mesh writes), axmp-mesher --export-regions on it, and solids.from_partition on the partition it writes. The mesher's export builds the geometry of the electromagnetic mesh (the half disk, the regions in order, the curves, the fragmentation) and writes, instead of a mesh, the partition of that geometry to the info path of its input: regions (the design's regions and the background air, each with its attr, its area_m2 and its volume_m3, computed from the exact curves), entities (every curve with the keys above; side names a region, air for the background, or exterior beyond the outer arc and the axis) and faces. The tags are those of the mesh of the same input. A contour's elliptical segment, a B-spline in gmsh, is an ellipse with the contour's own centre and axes. The mesher exits with status 1 and {"ok": false, "error": ...} in that file when the construction fails, and refuses inputs of the bounded and plane modes (use the bounded mode's own info file with resolve_only: it carries the same keys). A 3D input has its own partition (3D designs).

  • composition: {material: block}, the block of Materials with an optional density in kg/m3. Each region takes its design material; the background region takes the material named air (the design's vacuum material of that name, or the design's own definition of air). Entries for materials no region uses are ignored; sheets (curves) have no volume and need no entry; disabled regions are not in the partition.
  • The density of a material is the design's, as the electromagnetic parser resolves it (iron 7874, copper 8960 and nb 8570 are built in; an expression is evaluated), when it is positive; otherwise the density of the block. Two different positive values are particle.composition_invalid (naming the material and both values); none is particle.density_missing; a used material without a block is particle.composition_missing.
  • solids: a path; the solids document is also written there as solids.json. chord_tol_m is passed to the conversion, and so are its warnings.
  • workdir: keeps regions_in.json (the mesher input) and regions.json (the partition, the mesher's info) there. Without it a temporary directory is used and removed; nothing is written in the current directory.
  • mesher: the program (default: $AXMP_MESHER, else the package's).

Refused, with nothing written: a model document (model.em_only_operation); a 3D design with mesh.symmetry, a design on an imported mesh (mesh.file) and a mesher without the export mode (particle.partition_unavailable); a mesher that cannot be run or loaded, as the model path reports it (build.requires_mesher, with the loader's message); a planar or cross-section design (particle.planar_not_offered); a mesher run that fails (mesh.generation_failed, the message carrying the mesher's error and the last lines of its log in the hint; with workdir the log stays there as regions_mesher.log). The input is made by the code that axmp mesh runs, which also meshes the design once into a temporary directory.

docs.title: 3D designs
docs.text:
Design.export_gdml also exports a 3D electromagnetic design ("symmetry": "3d"), with the same arguments and the same composition rules. Every volume becomes a tessellated solid: a closed triangulated surface, which Geant4 builds as a G4TessellatedSolid. The route is the design's 3D mesher input (the mesh3d_in.json that axmp mesh writes, made by a library function that the 3D engine also uses, compiled into every build: the sequential build exports 3D designs too, and the engine is not run), axmp-mesher --export-regions on it and solids.from_partition on the partition. Each rank of a parallel program (mpirun -n 4 python script.py) exports on its own, with the same files; nothing is collective. The mesher runs only with the export flag, never for an electromagnetic mesh. The engine's own refusals of a design (sheets, in a 3D design) are reported as themselves. A design reduced by symmetry planes (mesh.symmetry) is refused with particle.partition_unavailable: a reduced model is not the device.

The mesher builds the 3D geometry as for the electromagnetic mesh (the solids, the domain sphere, the infinity shell, the fragmentation, the region of each volume by priority) and writes, instead of a mesh, the 3D partition to the info path of its input. The infinity shell is not part of it: the transport's domain ends at the domain sphere, the inner radius domain_radius. The conductors that the electromagnetic mesh removes (remove_pec) are volumes of the partition. The file has geometry "3d", domain_radius, domain_center, diagonal_m (of the union of the faces' boxes), tolerance_m (1e-9 × diagonal_m), chord_tol_m and:

  • regions: {name: {"attr", "volume_m3"}} for the design's regions and the background air; volume_m3 is the exact volume (OpenCASCADE's).
  • entities: one record per face, in the order of tag, with dim 2, side ([A, B]: the face's triangles' normal points from the region A into the region B; air for the background, exterior beyond the domain sphere, where the infinity shell was), curves ([]), axis (false), type (gmsh's surface type in lower case: plane, cylinder, cone, sphere, torus, bspline_surface, ...), lo and hi (a box that holds the face), point and normal (a point of the face and the unit normal of the surface there, turned like the triangles) and area_m2.
  • volumes: [{"tag", "region", "shells", "volume_m3"}], every volume but the shell's. tag is the volume's tag in the mesh of the same input. shells lists signed face tags, the outer shell first: +tag where the volume is the face's side[0] (the triangles' normal points out of it), -tag where it is side[1]. A shell with its faces turned by their signs is a closed manifold surface oriented outwards (every edge used once in each direction in the shell); a cavity is an inner shell. Faces belong to one shell when an edge of the shell pairs them, so the air around two boxes that meet along an edge has a shell for each. A domain without regions exports the air alone (one volume).
  • triangulation: {"nodes": [[x, y, z], ...], "faces": [{"tag", "triangles", "sagitta_m"}, ...]}. One node list serves the whole partition; each face is triangulated once and listed once (the volumes on its two sides use the same triangles, one with the reversed orientation, and the faces that meet at a curve share its nodes, so that coordinates agree bit for bit with no matching tolerance). sagitta_m is the largest distance of a triangle's centroid or edge midpoint from the face (0 for a plane).

The chord tolerance. chord_tol_m is the largest distance a triangle may lie from its face. It is the input's key chord_tol_m (the chord_tol_m of Design.export_gdml), by default min(1 mm, 1e-4 × diagonal_m). The triangulation is the export's own, made for that tolerance, and depends on the geometry and the tolerance only, not on the sizes of the electromagnetic mesh. A region's triangulated volume differs from its exact one only under the triangles of curved faces (reported per region, and warned about above VOLUME_WARN: lower chord_tol_m); planar regions are exact to rounding.

The solids. One solid per volume, of kind tessellated with params {"vertices_m": [[x, y, z], ...], "triangles": [[i, j, k], ...]}: the triangles of the volume's outer shell, counter-clockwise seen from outside, with its own vertex list copied bit for bit from the partition's nodes, so that solids that touch have the same facets on the face between them. Position and rotation are zero (the vertices are absolute); discretized is true and sagitta_m the largest of the outer shell's faces. Names are <region>_<k> in a geometric order. The volumes in a cavity of a volume (inside one of its inner shells, directly or as a cluster of volumes touching across faces of their outer shells) are that volume's daughters; a volume in no cavity is a daughter of the world, a vacuum orb around every node. In the report, volume_solids_m3 is the volume of the region's solids minus their daughters', which is the triangulated volume of the region.

Thin layers. The triangles are chords of the exact surfaces, so a layer thinner than about the chord tolerance cannot be represented: the chords of its two surfaces cross. The conversion refuses such a partition with particle.partition_invalid (the message names the region, the hint says to lower chord_tol_m well below the layer's thickness) when a daughter's triangulated surface is not inside its mother's, when two siblings overlap, or when a solid's own triangles cross each other. Triangles that two solids share exactly are contact, not overlap. The mesher still exports the partition at any tolerance (its sides are facts of the topology), and the same partition converts at a finer chord_tol_m. The checks use a sweep over the triangles' boxes, exact piercing tests of triangle edges against triangles (the tolerance is tolerance_m) and ray casting for containment; on the window-frame dipole (29 000 triangles) they take about 2 s. Pairs of triangles are found with a uniform 3D grid, so the time grows about as the number of triangles; a solid that is star-shaped about the centre of its box (a ball, a box, a cylinder: every triangle faces away from the centre and their solid angles add up to 4 pi) cannot cross itself and skips the self-crossing test. A fine chord_tol_m costs mostly in triangles, not in the checks: the count of a curved face grows as 1 / chord_tol_m (a sphere of 0.5 m radius: 64 000 triangles at 1.5e-4 m, 425 000 at 3.3e-5 m, converted in 1.7 s and 8.9 s with the self-crossing test forced on, 0.2 s and 1.1 s without), and the export, the JSON files and Geant4's tessellated solids grow with it.

GDML. A tessellated solid is a <tessellated name="<gdml_name>_solid" lunit="m"> of <triangular vertex1= vertex2= vertex3= type="ABSOLUTE"/> in the list's order and orientation; its vertices are <position unit="m"> entries of <define> named <gdml_name>_v<k>, written with 17 digits. axmp-transport --geometry builds a G4TessellatedSolid of G4TriangularFacet (ABSOLUTE, lengths in m) set closed, after checking that the triangles close (every edge once in each direction) and enclose a positive volume: Geant4 only warns about an open solid, the program refuses it as an invalid file (exit status 2, the solid named).

Every 3D volume is tessellated, including the primitives: a native solid that touches a tessellated one across a curved face would overlap it by the sagitta, which Geant4's overlap check (a tolerance of zero) refuses.

docs.title: The solids
docs.text:
Each face becomes one solid, a full revolution about the z axis:

  1. Notches at the axis are filled. The solid of a face is the revolution of its outer loop with every notch at the axis filled: of the parts of the loop between consecutive points on the axis, the one that runs upwards is kept and the others are replaced by the axis. Whatever lies in a notch (a face, or a hole of the domain) becomes a daughter of the solid, as whatever lies in a hole does. This is what makes a sphere on the axis exact: the face around it is a full tube, and the sphere is placed in it.
  2. The kind of solid. One closed circle off the axis is a torus; one half circle centred on the axis, its ends on the axis, is an orb; straight edges that make a rectangle (after merging collinear edges) a tube; anything else a genericPolycone, exact when its edges are straight and discretized when it has arcs. A circle split into several curves, an ellipse and a fillet are polycones.
  3. Holes of the domain are vacuum. The boundary curves of the domain, followed with the domain on their left, form closed chains (or chains from the axis to the axis, closed along it). A chain that turns clockwise encloses a part of the exterior: it becomes a vacuum solid void_<k> (G4_Galactic), so that a hole is never filled with the material around it.
  4. The mother of a face or a void is the smallest filled loop that contains it; one that nothing contains is a daughter of the world. Siblings do not overlap and every daughter lies inside its mother by construction, provided no two curves come closer than about the chord tolerance (the chords of a curve stray from it by up to its sagitta). The conversion checks it: when a layer is thinner than that, so that a face or a void would lose its place in the tree, a daughter would leave its mother, two siblings would overlap or a polycone would cross itself, it refuses the partition with particle.partition_invalid, whose hint is to lower chord_tol_m well below the layer's thickness. It never writes a list without a face or with overlapping solids. Curves that touch convert when the discretized chords stay on their own side (two circles or ellipses touching from outside, a torus on the edge of a box, an ellipse inscribed in a box). Where a discretized curve is concave towards the other solid (a shape touching the inside of an ellipse, say), the chords pass through that solid by about 0.8 of the chord tolerance at every tolerance, so lowering chord_tol_m does not help: the partition is refused, and the curves must be separated there by a few chord tolerances. A face whose outline passes twice through one point (a pinch: a notch whose tip touches the face's own boundary) is refused too, naming the region and the point, because whether Geant4 builds such a polycone depends on rounding in its crossing test; separate the touching boundaries. The checks work to 1e-12 of the partition's diagonal but never above 5e-13 m (half of Geant4's overlap tolerance), so that a partition admitted here is not refused by Geant4's overlap check.
  5. The world is a vacuum tube (G4_Galactic) centred at the origin, enclosing the partition with a margin of 1e-3 of its diagonal.
  6. Names. The solids of a region are <region>_0, <region>_1, ... in a geometric order (their bounding box, their area, then their vertices); the voids void_0, void_1, ... (skipping a name that the solids of a region called void already have); the world world. Any region or material name is accepted: the names that GDML and Geant4 use are mapped from them (gdml_name, below).

Discretization. Every arc of a polycone is cut into chords once, from its curve, and every solid that has it uses the same points, so neighbours share their vertices bit for bit and leave no gap or sliver. The end points are the partition's; the points between are at equal steps of the curve parameter. A circular arc of radius R and sweep θ is cut into the fewest equal angles N whose sagitta R (1 - cos(θ/2N)) is within the tolerance; an elliptical arc uses the same rule with its major semi-axis, whose sagitta bounds the true one. The tolerance chord_tol of a region is min(1 µm, 1e-5 × the diagonal of the box of its curves); a curve between two regions uses the smaller of their two; chord_tol_m= sets every region's. Tori and orbs are never discretized.

docs.title: solids.json
docs.text:
{"schema": "axionmultiphysics.solids/1", "generator": "axionmultiphysics <version>", "geometry": "axisymmetric",
 "units": {"length": "m", "angle": "deg", "density": "kg/m3", "volume": "m3", "mass": "kg"},
 "chord_tol_m": null, "world": "world", "materials": [...], "solids": [...], "regions": {...}, "warnings": []}

The file holds no time, host name or path, and the same partition gives the same bytes on every run (strict JSON, UTF-8, numbers as the shortest text that reads back as the same double).

  • materials: the materials that some region uses, sorted by name: {"name", "gdml_name", "density_kg_m3", "composition"} and, when given, mean_excitation_eV, state, T_K, pressure_Pa. composition is {"nist": "G4_..."} or {"elements": {symbol: value}, "by": "mass" | "atoms"}.
  • solids: every solid after its mother (the world first, children in name order), each {"name", "gdml_name", "kind", "params", "mother", "position_m", "rotation_deg", "region", "material", "discretized", "sagitta_m"}. region and material are the document's names. position_m is relative to the mother; rotation_deg is [0, 0, 0] for an axisymmetric design. region is null for the world and the voids, whose material is G4_Galactic. sagitta_m is the largest sagitta of the chords in the solid (0 when none).
  • The parameters of each kind are named as GDML's attributes, with a unit suffix:
kind params frame tube rmin_m, rmax_m, z_m (the full length), startphi_deg, deltaphi_deg its centre torus rmin_m (0), rmax_m, rtor_m, startphi_deg, deltaphi_deg the centre of its circle orb r_m its centre genericPolycone startphi_deg, deltaphi_deg, rz_m ([[r, z], ...], counter-clockwise) the origin: its points are absolute tessellated (3D lists) vertices_m ([[x, y, z], ...]), triangles ([[i, j, k], ...], counter-clockwise seen from outside) the origin: its vertices are absolute

Values that the partition states (radii, vertices) are copied bit for bit. - regions: per region with faces, in document order: material, density_kg_m3, solids (its solids' names), volume_m3, volume_solids_m3, volume_rel_diff, mass_kg, mass_solids_kg, mass_rel_diff, sagitta_max_m, chord_tol_m. - warnings: one entry {"code": "particle.volume_deficit", "region", ...} per region above the threshold.

docs.title: The volume and mass report
docs.text: volume_m3 is the volume of the exact solid of revolution of the region's faces: by Pappus' theorem, π times the closed integral of r² dz around every loop of every face, evaluated in closed form on lines and arcs from the curve parameters. volume_solids_m3 is what the solids hold: for each of the region's solids, its volume minus its daughters' (the closed forms Geant4 uses: a tube, a torus, a sphere, and the sum of cone frusta of a polycone). volume_rel_diff is volume_solids_m3 / volume_m3 - 1; it is zero to rounding for exact solids, and for discretized ones the chords move the volume by at most 2π r_max s L (s the sagitta, L the length of the curved boundary). The masses are the volumes times the material's density. When |volume_rel_diff| or |mass_rel_diff| exceeds VOLUME_WARN (1e-4), the region is warned about (SolidsWarning, message particle.volume_deficit: region '<name>' ...) and listed in warnings: lower chord_tol_m.

docs.title: Materials
docs.text:
A material in the transport's domain needs a particle block and a density; nothing is ever treated as vacuum (vacuum is written explicitly, as {"nist": "G4_Galactic"}):

"iron":  {"density": 7874.0, "particle": {"nist": "G4_Fe"}},
"steel": {"density": 7930.0, "particle": {"elements": {"Fe": 0.70, "Cr": 0.19, "Ni": 0.11}, "by": "mass"}},
"pe":    {"density": 940.0,  "particle": {"elements": {"C": 1, "H": 2}, "by": "atoms", "mean_excitation_eV": 57.4}}
  • nist: the name of a NIST material of Geant4 (G4_...); the material is that composition at the document's density.
  • elements with by: "mass": mass fractions, positive and summing to 1 within 1e-9 (they are not renormalized); with by: "atoms": positive integer atom counts. Elements are given by their symbols, from H to Bh (Z = 1 to 107, the elements Geant4's NIST tables build); a heavier element is refused, so that no exported file names an element Geant4 cannot build.
  • Optional: mean_excitation_eV, state (solid, liquid or gas), T_K, pressure_Pa (positive).
  • NIST compositions are resolved before a run. from_partition writes a NIST composition as a material of one component (the NIST material) at the document's density, and Geant4 would then compute its mean excitation energy from the elements by Bragg additivity and set its state from the density, instead of using NIST's values (water 69.0 eV, solid, instead of 78.0 eV, liquid; NaI 400 eV instead of 452 eV). The transport therefore resolves every NIST composition against the Geant4 it runs with (particles.resolve_materials, which reads axmp-transport --nist; the driver runs it before every run and writes the resolved list to the run's exchange/solids.json):
    • a material whose block is exactly {"nist": X} at X's own density (within 1e-9, relative) becomes the NIST material itself: its solids name X, the GDML file references X, and the material record is dropped when no solid uses it (the region keeps its document material name in regions);
    • any other NIST composition keeps its one component and takes X's mean_excitation_eV and state where the document gives none (written as <MEE> and state= in GDML, set the same way natively);
    • a density more than 1 % from NIST's warns particle.density_differs_from_nist (the document's density is used).

The residual of the second case, measured with Geant4 11.4.3's G4EmCalculator (total dE/dx at NIST's density against the NIST material itself):

material 1 GeV/c muons 100 GeV/c muons 10 MeV protons 1 MeV electrons G4_WATER +1.01 % 0.00 % +0.58 % +0.61 % G4_SODIUM_IODIDE +1.41 % +0.06 % +1.23 % +0.45 % G4_CESIUM_IODIDE +1.69 % +0.04 % +1.61 % +0.40 % G4_BGO +1.99 % +0.10 % 0 +1.18 % G4_POLYSTYRENE +0.82 % 0 +1.05 % +0.79 % G4_KAPTON +1.02 % 0 +0.81 % +0.98 % G4_AIR, G4_PbWO4, G4_lAr within 0.09 % within 0.09 % within 0.09 % within 0.09 % G4_Fe, G4_Si 0 0 +0.16 %, +0.21 % 0

It comes from data Geant4 looks up by the NIST material's name (the density-effect table, ICRU 90 water, proton stopping tables), which only the NIST material itself carries. Where it matters, use the NIST density, or give an explicit element composition with mean_excitation_eV. - A document material may not have a name that starts with G4_: that prefix always names a NIST material. - The density is the material's density in kg/m3 and is always the one used. (Comparing it with the NIST density of a NIST material is a check of the transport set-up, where Geant4's tables are.)

docs.title: GDML
docs.text:
