write_gdml(doc, path) writes the same list as GDML (define, materials, solids, structure, setup), so that any Geant4 application can read it. Three rules make Geant4 read from it the same numbers as axmp-transport builds from solids.json:

  1. 17 significant digits. Every number is written with 17 significant digits (%.17g), which reads back as the same double (Geant4's own writer uses 15, which does not). Lengths are in m and angles in deg, units Geant4 multiplies exactly as the native path does; a density is <D value=... unit="kg/m3"/> with the document's value.
  2. NIST by name, never defined. The file defines no element, no isotope and no material with a NIST name: Geant4's reader prefers a file's definition to its NIST table, which would change the material's data. Every document material is a material of the file, named by its gdml_name, with its density and its components: one <fraction n="1" ref="G4_Fe"/> for a NIST composition, <fraction n=... ref="Fe"/> by mass, <composite n=... ref="H"/> by atoms (Geant4's NIST manager resolves the elements from their symbols), after T, P, MEE and D. The world and the voids reference G4_Galactic; so does every solid whose material a resolved list names directly (G4_WATER at NIST's density, say): its volume's materialref is the NIST name.
  3. Rotations are written as the document's angles, x then y then z (none in an axisymmetric design).

One volume per solid, named by the solid's gdml_name, is defined after its daughters (the world last); each daughter is a physvol with a position in m. The volume's solid, placement and position are named after it, with _solid, _pv and _pos.

Names in the file. A GDML name is an XML ID: ASCII letters, digits, _, . and -, not starting with a digit, unique across the file; and Geant4's reader cuts a name where it contains 0x. A document may name its regions and materials as it likes (316L steel, 1st, world), so each solid and each material carries a gdml_name: its own name when that is valid, contains no 0x, does not start with G4_ and collides with no other name of the file (including the _solid, _pv and _pos names, and Default, the name of the file's setup); otherwise the name with every other character replaced by _, a _ in front of a leading digit, 0x written 0_x, and _1, _2, ... appended until it is unique. Solids are named before materials, each set in name order, so the mapping depends only on the names, never on the order of the input. axmp-transport gives its Geant4 volumes and materials the same names, and its placements the names Geant4's GDML reader gives them (<gdml_name>_pv, and <gdml_name>_PV for the world's), so a GDML application and the native path name everything alike; solids.json keeps the document's names beside them. With these names the file follows the GDML schema of Geant4 11.4.3 (the schema is not part of this repository).

docs.title: The geometry mode of axmp-transport
docs.text:
axmp-transport --geometry solids.json

builds the list in Geant4 (see Particle transport for building the program): the materials through Geant4's NIST manager as above (a NIST composition is a material of the document's density with one component, the NIST material; a solid whose material is a NIST name uses that NIST material), one G4Tubs, G4Torus, G4Orb, G4GenericPolycone or (3D lists) G4TessellatedSolid per solid, one logical volume per solid placed in its mother's, with the lengths read in metres and the angles in degrees, and every volume and material named by its gdml_name. It then runs Geant4's overlap check (CheckOverlaps, 1000 points per placement, a tolerance of zero) on every placement and prints one JSON document on stdout:

{"ok": true,
 "volumes": [{"name", "g4_name", "placement", "region", "material", "solid_volume_m3", "volume_m3", "density_kg_m3", "mass_kg"}],
 "materials": [{"name", "g4_name", "density_kg_m3", "mean_excitation_eV", "state", "T_K", "pressure_Pa",
                "elements"}],
 "overlaps": []}

name, region and material are the names of the solids list, g4_name the name the Geant4 volume or material holds (the gdml_name; a NIST material keeps its name) and placement the name of the volume's placement. solid_volume_m3 is Geant4's volume of the solid, volume_m3 that minus its daughters', density_kg_m3 the density of its Geant4 material and mass_kg their product. They agree with the report's volume_solids_m3 and mass_solids_kg within 1e-9. materials lists every material the volumes use (G4_Galactic included) as Geant4 built it: its density, mean excitation energy (the document's mean_excitation_eV, or the one Geant4 computes from the elements), state (solid, liquid or gas; Geant4 makes a material of undefined state solid above 10 kg/m3 and a gas below), temperature and pressure (293.15 K and 101325 Pa unless the document gives them) and elements, the mass fraction of each element. These are what a GDML application reading the exported file must reproduce. Every value is converted from Geant4's units once, on output.

An overlap refuses the geometry: exit status 3 and {"ok": false, "code": "particle.geometry_overlap", "error": ..., "overlaps": [{"volume", "mother", "message"}]}. A file that is not a valid solids list is refused with exit status 2, a message on stderr and nothing on stdout; that includes a polycone that Geant4 refuses to build (an outline of almost no area, edges that cross, or fewer than three points left after Geant4 merges the vertices closer than its length tolerance, 1e-12 m, in both R and Z; Geant4's own message is on stderr) or one whose outline runs back over itself along a stretch of an edge (the program's own check). --check reports "geometry": true for a program that has this mode.

docs.title: Codes
docs.text:
code kind raised for particle.planar_not_offered error A planar partition: transport is offered for axisymmetric and 3D designs. particle.partition_unavailable error Design.export_gdml on a design whose partition cannot be exported in this version or with this mesher: a 3D design reduced by symmetry planes (mesh.symmetry), an imported mesh (mesh.file), or an axmp-mesher without --export-regions. particle.partition_invalid error A table that does not describe closed faces with exact curves (see The partition), or a layer thinner than about the chord tolerance, whose solids would overlap, cross themselves or lose their place in the tree (lower chord_tol_m). particle.composition_missing error A region without a material, a material that is not defined, or a material without a particle block. particle.density_missing error A material used by a region without a positive, finite density. particle.composition_invalid error A particle block that is not one of the forms above: an unknown key, both or neither of nist and elements, a nist name without G4_, by missing or not mass/atoms, an unknown element symbol or one heavier than Bh (Z = 107), mass fractions that are not positive or do not sum to 1, atom counts that are not positive integers, a state other than solid, liquid or gas, a non-positive mean_excitation_eV, T_K or pressure_Pa, or a document material named G4_...; for Design.export_gdml also a composition density that differs from the design's. particle.volume_deficit warning A region whose solids differ from the exact solid of revolution by more than VOLUME_WARN in volume or mass. particle.geometry_overlap error axmp-transport --geometry: Geant4's overlap check found a placement that leaves its mother or enters a sibling. particle.density_differs_from_nist warning particles.resolve_materials: a NIST composition whose density differs from NIST's by more than 1 %.

The messages name the region, the material, the element or the key concerned.

docs.title: Limits of this version
docs.text:
• Axisymmetric designs (full revolutions only) and 3D designs without symmetry planes; model documents come later.
  • A 3D design is exported as tessellated solids only (native solids for primitives are not offered), to the chord tolerance of the export. A layer thinner than the chord tolerance is refused by the conversion (see "Thin layers" in 3D designs); a very thin layer needs a fine chord_tol_m and a large triangulation.
  • The partition must carry the extended entity table (exact curve parameters and face loops). B-splines are not read: the mesher writes a contour's elliptical arc as an ellipse.
  • Design.export_gdml has no mesh.file route, and it meshes an axisymmetric design once to obtain the mesher's input (a 3D design is not meshed: its mesher input is written without the engine).
  • Elements up to Z = 107 only (Geant4's NIST tables build no heavier one).

docs.title: Designs and solvers
docs.text:
Lumped-element detectors and cavity haloscopes search for axion dark matter. In this guide we describe axionMultiPhysics designs and solvers.

A design is a JSON document describing geometry, materials, magnet windings, readout and mesh settings in SI units. Numeric fields accept expressions over named parameters; later regions replace earlier ones where they overlap, and unassigned space is air.

docs.title: Design file
docs.text:
We write, load and solve a complete JSON design, toroid.json, for a toroidal magnet with a superconducting pickup sheath to obtain coupling and inductance.

import axionmultiphysics as axmp

axmp.template("toroid", R=2.0, H=2.0).save("toroid.json")
design = axmp.load("toroid.json")
print(design.validate())
result = design.solve("runs/toroid")
print(result.Psi, result.L_p)

Validation reports ok: True and evaluated parameters, or identifies an invalid field. The solve returns coupling in \(\mathrm{H\,T\,m^2}\) and inductance in henries; we check mesh refinement and residuals before using them.

Top-level keys Purpose schema, name, symmetry Format, name and geometry dimension parameters Named numbers and expressions regions, curves, materials Volumes, sheets and material properties windings, circuits, background Static-field sources superconductors, pickup Constraints and readout mesh Element sizes and order fullwave, cavity Driven frequency sweeps or cavity modes scan, benchmarks, cost Sensitivity assumptions and cost metric

docs.title: Field models
docs.text:
axionMultiPhysics's magnetoquasistatic (MQS) solver neglects displacement current and is appropriate when the detector is small compared with the signal wavelength. Its full-wave solver retains displacement current to resolve radiation, resonances and frequency-dependent coupling. With time dependence \(e^{-i\omega t}\),

\[ \Psi(\omega)=\frac{1}{i\omega I}\int \mathbf E_I\cdot\mathbf B_{\rm lab}\,dV, \qquad L(\omega)=-\frac{\operatorname{Im}Z(\omega)}{\omega}. \]

Here \(\omega\) is angular frequency, \(\mathbf E_I\) is the field driven by pickup current \(I\), \(\mathbf B_{\rm lab}\) is the static field and \(Z\) is terminal impedance. Both quantities approach their MQS values at low frequency; negative inductance indicates a capacitive response.

We add "fullwave": {"frequencies": [1e5, 1e6, 1e7], "boundary": "radiation"} for a sweep in hertz; pec instead closes the domain with a perfect conductor. Each result.fullwave["sweep"] row reports f_Hz, Psi_abs and L_H.

Both models default to "symmetry": "axisymmetric", for rotationally symmetric geometry and excitation. We set "symmetry": "3d" for slits or localized feeds; this requires an MPI-enabled installation. Axisymmetric feeds are distributed uniformly around the axis. Eigenmode calculations are described in Cavity haloscopes.

docs.title: Tree-cotree solve
docs.text: The tree-cotree solve is beta. At low frequency, separating gradient fields from magnetic-flux-carrying fields avoids cancellation in the 3D full-wave matrix. We set AXMP_FW_SOLVER=strumpack and AXMP_FW_GAUGE=tree-cotree; this requires STRUMPACK, first-order Nédélec elements, real lossless materials and PEC on every boundary. We assess split_true_relative_residual; the factorization occupies one MPI rank.

docs.title: Multiport circuits and components
docs.text: axionmultiphysics.multiport.MultiportCircuit connects the detector impedance matrix to external loads, preserving the relative phases of axion-induced voltages. axionmultiphysics.multiport_components.LosslessTransmissionLine adds propagation delay and stored energy for distributed connections. We include only components absent from the FEM model, and supply reciprocal, passive impedances. We orient circuit branches along each gap's current profile; circuit current is opposite the current entering the FEM device.

docs.title: 3D ports and magnetic sources
docs.text: Each gap in fullwave.ports touches two conducting terminal patches; toward sets its current direction, while the primary pickup needs a conducting return through one body. Each sweep row contains Z_matrix_re_ohm, Z_matrix_im_ohm and coherent Psi_vector: the pickup comes first, matrix rows are measured ports and columns are driven ports. fullwave.source supplies an independent static field for the axion overlap (beta, below).

docs.title: Prescribed static source
docs.text: The prescribed static source is beta. For example, we add "boundary": "pec", "source": {"kind": "uniform", "B_T": [0, 1, 0]} inside fullwave for a \(1\,\mathrm T\) field along the global \(y\) axis. This replaces only the RF overlap field, leaving MQS energies and forces unchanged; it does not compute screening. With radiation boundaries, we use closed current segments inside the domain and check source quadrature as well as RF mesh convergence.

docs.title: Visualization
docs.text: Lumped-element axion experiments use static magnetic fields and pickup circuits. In this guide we use the axionMultiPhysics viewer to display detector materials and magnetic fields in a browser or Jupyter notebook. Axisymmetric designs have a revolved cutaway and a meridional section; full 3D designs show surfaces and field slices. We rotate, pan and zoom, then select a field quantity or probe a point.

docs.title: Viewing and saving a result
docs.text:
We display the result res from the quick start and save its HTML viewer and scene for later display.

res.show(height=520)
res.export_html("toroid.html")
scene = res.scene()
res.save_scene("scene.json")

show displays a notebook widget. The HTML file includes both the scene and viewer, so it can be opened or shared without a network connection. The scene is a Python dictionary; its JSON file stores geometry, sampled fields and results for later display without another solve.

We select Bmag for the static magnetic-field magnitude in tesla, or pickup_Bmag for the pickup field per ampere of readout current. The colour bar gives the units. Poloidal field lines in an axisymmetric scene follow contours of the flux function

\[ \psi = r A_\phi. \]

Here \(r\) is cylindrical radius and \(A_\phi\) is the azimuthal vector potential; psi has units \(\mathrm{Wb/rad}\). A purely toroidal field has no poloidal field lines. Line spacing depends on the chosen contour levels. Displayed fields are interpolated samples, so solver peak values can exceed the colour-bar maximum.

docs.title: Scenes and PNG snapshots
docs.text:
The viewer and renderer read the same axionmultiphysics.scene/1 format. Its regions describe materials, field or slices hold sampled quantities, summary contains solver results, and design stores the input document. Coordinates are in metres: radius and height for axisymmetric scenes, Cartesian coordinates for full 3D scenes. A scene contains display samples, not the full finite-element solution.

We render the saved scene as a PNG to view the pickup-field magnitude.

from axionmultiphysics.render import save_png

save_png("scene.json", "pickup.png", view="section",
         quantity="pickup_Bmag", log_scale=True)

This writes a pickup-field image using a software renderer, without a browser or GPU. We use view="3d" for a cutaway and quantity="none" for materials only. Logarithmic colours show magnitudes; we use a linear scale when a component's sign matters. We set matching vmin and vmax when comparing images, width and height for pixel dimensions, and annotate=False to hide the results panel.

The API reference lists display options.

docs.title: Error codes of the model document (beta)
docs.text:
Most findings about a model document (a design with a physics section) carry a code: a stable identifier of the form area.problem, for programs and assistants to act on, beside the message, the JSON pointer and the hint that people read. This page lists every code of the model path. A few findings carry no code, and for them the message, the pointer and the hint are all there is: the ones that an electromagnetic design can also have (a required field that is missing, a field that does not exist, a value of the wrong type or out of its range), an expression that cannot be read or evaluated, an unknown value of symmetry, of a study type, of a coupling strategy or of a continuation scale, and an internal failure of the validation. Model documents are beta: this version validates a model document (axmp validate, Design.validate()), resolves its geometry (axmp resolve), explains it (axmp explain), patches it (axmp patch), lists and checks its named boundaries (axmp boundaries) and meshes a planar or axisymmetric one (axmp mesh, axmp.mesh); it solves none (no route is implemented), so a code may still be renamed. Some codes are raised for electromagnetic designs too: model.section_needs_physics (a section of a model document in a design without physics), the refusals of an arc path (geometry.arc_span, geometry.arc_degenerate, geometry.arc_negative_r) and mesh.tangled, when a 2D mesh with a tangled curved element is read.

A finding has one of four kinds:

kind meaning error The document is wrong, and is refused. unavailable The document is valid; this version or this build cannot solve it. deferred A check that needs the resolved geometry or an imported mesh file, and runs when that is built or read. warning The document is valid; something about it is worth knowing.

This version raises 107 codes and names 3 more that a later version raises. The types, coupling terms and routes that the codes refer to are in the physics catalogue.

docs.title: Boundaries and selectors (boundary)
docs.text: code kind raised for boundary.between_overlap error A between selector whose two domains share a region, where the direction of its normal is undefined. boundary.cycle error Boundaries that name one another in a cycle (in a name, a union, a difference or an except). boundary.empty_selection error, deferred A named boundary that selects nothing: an error of the check on the resolved boundaries, which axmp boundaries and axmp mesh run; axmp validate does not resolve the boundaries (that needs the mesher, or the info file of an imported mesh) and reports it as deferred. boundary.imported_mesh_selector deferred A geometric boundary selector on an imported mesh, whose boundaries are the groups of its info file; resolved when the file is read. boundary.name_collision error One name used by two of the regions, curves, domains and boundaries, which share a namespace. boundary.partial_match warning A where filter leaves out an edge that satisfies it in part, in a boundary that selects other edges: the filter keeps an edge only when the whole edge satisfies it. boundary.reserved_name error One of the reserved names axis, exterior and remaining used where it has no meaning. boundary.selector_grammar error A boundary selector that is not one of the selector forms, or a filter on a form that takes none. boundary.unknown_name error A boundary or a curve that the document does not define.

docs.title: build (build)
docs.text: code kind raised for build.requires_fluids unavailable An instance mesh handed to the fluids engines (im.fluids_mesh()) in a build without the fluids module: a wheel from PyPI or the sequential source build; the MPI source build has it. build.requires_mesher unavailable A model document with a geometry in an installation whose mesher does not run: a wheel installed without the mesh extra, or a mesher whose libraries are missing; the validation reports it, and the commands that mesh refuse the document. Design.export_gdml refuses with it a mesher that cannot be run or loaded.

docs.title: Reserved
docs.text:
Codes that this version names, in the route table, in the details of a deferred finding or in the check on the resolved boundaries that a later version runs, and that no path of this version raises.

code kind meaning internal.route_table_out_of_date error An engine refused what validation accepted: a defect of the route table, not of the document. physics.option_not_offered error An option value that a route refuses, for a physics that is neither a flow nor a heat instance; no route of this version refuses one. route.single_rank unavailable A route that runs on one MPI rank, asked to run on several.

docs.title: Physics catalogue (beta)
docs.text:
The physics catalogue is the registry that model documents (designs with a physics section) are validated against (axmp validate); this version does not solve them: the physics types, the coupling terms between them, and the route table, one row per combination of physics, couplings, geometry class and study type that an engine of this version solves, with what the row offers and what it needs. It is compiled into every build and is the same in each, so a document validates the same way everywhere. Everything on this page is beta, and no route is implemented in this version: a model document is validated and resolved, and a planar or axisymmetric one is meshed (axmp mesh), but none is solved.

Print it with axmp physics (--routes adds the route table, --type T restricts it to one type, --all prints the details, --json the machine form of schema axionmultiphysics.physics_catalogue/1), or in Python with axionmultiphysics.physics(routes=True, type=None).

• Status: not implemented yet.
  • Physics: fluid.incompressible; couplings: none; geometry: planar; study: stationary.
  • Selected by: equation = stokes.
  • Engine: StokesSolver.
  • Needs: the mesher, an MPI build, the fluids library, any number of ranks.
  • Condition kinds offered (fluid.incompressible): wall, inlet, outlet, open, traction, slip, symmetry.
  • Not offered (fluid.incompressible): periodic: not_exposed: the engine needs a topologically periodic mesh, and the instance mesh has no boundary element on an interior face; exposing it takes a periodic instance mesh, the partition rule's exception for the partner and matching nodes on the two sides (roadmap item 'periodic flow').
  • Options (fluid.incompressible): equation: stokes (default `);viscous_form:stress,laplacian(defaultstress);order:2(default2`).

  • Force output: physical_reaction.
  • Layer rules: geometry_order_exceeds_field_order.
  • a force output with the Laplacian viscous form needs one viscosity over the instance (the engine's physical reaction is defined for a constant viscosity only).
  • periodic conditions are not exposed yet (roadmap item 'periodic flow').
  • any number of MPI ranks for the solve; outputs and point sampling on rank 0 from the saved solution.

• Status: not implemented yet.
  • Physics: heat.transfer; couplings: none; geometry: planar; study: stationary.
  • Engine: transport::ScalarTransport.
  • Needs: the mesher, an MPI build, the fluids library, at most 1 rank.
  • Condition kinds offered (heat.transfer): temperature, heat_flux, total_flux, convection, insulation, outflow.
  • Not offered with advective_form=conservative_divergence (heat.transfer): total_flux: engine_refuses.
  • Not offered with advective_form=conservative_flux (heat.transfer): heat_flux: engine_refuses.
  • Not offered with advective_form=conservative_flux (heat.transfer): outflow: layer_rule: outflow_with_conservative_flux.
  • Not offered with advective_form=convective (heat.transfer): total_flux: engine_refuses.
  • Options (heat.transfer): order: 1, 2 (default 2); stabilization: none (default none); advective_form: convective, conservative_divergence, conservative_flux (default convective).
  • Material blocks (heat.transfer): thermal.
  • One expression over the instance (heat.transfer): thermal.k_W_mK, heat_source.
  • Element types: triangle.
  • Layer rules: outflow_with_conservative_flux, per_depth_keys, geometry_order_exceeds_field_order.
  • one MPI rank.
  • triangles only (the transport operator's constructor refuses other elements).
  • thermal.k_W_mK and the heat source are one expression over the instance until the transport operator takes data per region.
  • stabilization supg is refused: there is no velocity for it.
  • without advection the three advective forms are one operator, and the condition kinds still depend on advective_form (the transport operator checks them against the form).

docs.title: flow_then_heat_planar
docs.text:
• Status: not implemented yet.
  • Physics: fluid.incompressible, heat.transfer; couplings: advection; geometry: planar; study: stationary.
  • Engine: the flow row's engine (StokesSolver or NavierStokesSolver), then transport::ScalarTransport with the finite-element velocity.
  • Needs: the mesher, an MPI build, the fluids library, at most 1 rank.
  • Coupling strategies: one_way (default one_way).
  • Condition kinds offered (heat.transfer): temperature, heat_flux, total_flux, convection, insulation, outflow.
  • Not offered with advective_form=conservative_divergence (heat.transfer): total_flux: engine_refuses.
  • Not offered with advective_form=conservative_flux (heat.transfer): heat_flux: engine_refuses.
  • Not offered with advective_form=conservative_flux (heat.transfer): outflow: layer_rule: outflow_with_conservative_flux.
  • Not offered with advective_form=convective (heat.transfer): total_flux: engine_refuses.
  • Options (heat.transfer): order: 1, 2 (default 2); stabilization: none, supg (default none); advective_form: convective, conservative_divergence, conservative_flux (default convective).
  • Material blocks (fluid.incompressible): fluid.
  • Material blocks (heat.transfer): thermal, thermal.cp_J_kgK, density.
  • Uniform over the instance (heat.transfer): density, thermal.cp_J_kgK.
  • One expression over the instance (heat.transfer): thermal.k_W_mK, heat_source.
  • Element types: triangle.
  • Equal domains: every instance of the row has the same domain.
  • Layer rules: insulation_on_throughflow, outflow_with_conservative_flux, per_depth_keys, geometry_order_exceeds_field_order, uniform_capacity_in_stagnant_part.
  • Solver settings (fluid.incompressible): those of the row of its own type that the instance's options select in this geometry.
  • one MPI rank.
  • triangles only (the transport operator's constructor refuses other elements).
  • thermal.k_W_mK and the heat source are one expression over the instance until the transport operator takes data per region.
  • the flow instance is checked against the Stokes or steady Navier-Stokes row of the same geometry that its equation selects, and solved first; its solver settings are those of that row.
  • the flow and heat instances have the same domain (one mesh, no interpolation).
  • density and thermal.cp_J_kgK are one constant over the instance, on a Stokes flow too.
  • stabilization supg needs straight elements, for the flow as well (one master mesh).
  • triangles only for the flow as well (one master mesh).
  • the condition kinds depend on advective_form.
  • no force output on this row.

docs.title: Layer rules
docs.text:
Rules of this layer that are stricter than the engine on purpose; each route lists the ones it applies.

rule what it refuses insulation_on_throughflow insulation is refused on a boundary that the advecting velocity crosses (heat.insulation_on_throughflow); the engine takes a zero flux anywhere outflow_with_conservative_flux outflow is refused with the conservative_flux form, where a zero total flux would block the advected heat (on a row without advection too, so that the name means the same on every heat row); the engine takes it as a zero flux and only the Python binding refuses the name, which this layer mirrors force_with_laplacian_form with the Laplacian viscous form a force output is accepted on walls at rest only (output.force_needs_stress_form), and needs one viscosity over the instance per_depth_keys an absolute input is written per metre of depth in a planar model (current_A_m, P_W_m) and as the 3D total otherwise (current_A, P_W) (model.per_depth_key) geometry_order_exceeds_field_order mesh.geometry_order may not exceed the smallest field order of the instances (model.geometry_order_exceeds_field_order) uniform_capacity_in_stagnant_part density and thermal.cp_J_kgK are one constant over an advected heat instance, in its stagnant parts as well, although a steady solve needs the capacity only where the velocity is not zero

docs.title: Particle transport validation (beta)
docs.text:
Particle transport (axionmultiphysics.particles and axmp-transport, see the guide) is beta. This page lists every check of the transport against an independent reference, what its last run measured, with its seed and number of events, and what is not checked. The checks are the tests tests/test_particles_transport.py, tests/test_particles_demo.py and tests/test_particles_driver.py; the references are written from physics and the design note in tests/_particles_ref.py, never from the implementation.

Run: Geant4 11.4.3 (multithreaded, tasking run manager), FTFP_BERT, production cut 0.7 mm, Geant4's default integrator (G4TDormandPrince45 with G4IntegrationDriver, deltaChord 0.25 mm, deltaOneStep 0.01 mm, deltaIntersection 1 um, epsilon 5e-5 to 1e-3), the sequential build of the package, AMD nodes of the cluster's cm1 and cm2 partitions (identical values on both), AXMP_SLOW=1. A single track is deterministic; every other number is Monte Carlo, given with its statistical error (one standard deviation: of the binomial count; of a standard deviation from N samples, 1/sqrt(2(N - 1)) relative; of a Gaussian core of N events, by 200 bootstrap resamplings of the events, 0.9 % relative at N = 1e4, about 1.35 / sqrt(2N), which is the value given for P5). Tolerances are the design note's ceilings or the tests' own; the measured value is given beside them.

docs.title: Reproducibility and statistics
docs.text:
row case measured S1 200 MeV electrons showering in 2 cm of Fe in 1 T (1000 events, 5 chunks, seed 7): 1 against 4 threads, 1 against 3 processes, the same seed twice, a run extended from 700 events (a short last chunk) every chunk array, the merged 128-bit tallies and results.json bitwise equal; per-event hit limits reached and the same S1 a chunk run alone, after other chunks, and in a 25 000-event chunk (beyond Geant4's refill of its seeds at 10 000); 1 and 4 threads bitwise equal; the first number of each event equals the MixMax references of the hello mode S1 a stop rule (2 % on the mean deposit, 80 planned chunks) with 1 and 4 workers the same prefix and results.json S1 81 one-event chunks of a 1 GeV electron in 20 cm of Pb with a quantum of (E + m) / 2^63 x 1.1 the 128-bit batch sums exceed 2^63 and equal the exact integer sums of the chunks S2 10 seeds x 2000 muons at 1 GeV/c in 1 cm of Fe, mean deposit chi2 = 13.99 for 9 degrees of freedom (P(chi2 >) = 0.12) S3 1e7 isotropic geantinos (seed 2024, 1000 chunks of 1e4, 8 processes), a disk of 10 deg half-angle the 1 sigma interval of the mean covers (1 - cos 10 deg) / 2 in (69.6 +- 1.5) % of the chunks, Clopper-Pearson's in (71.8 +- 1.4) % (asserted 68.3 +- 5.9 % and >= 62.4 %); acceptance (7.590 +- 0.027)e-3 against 7.596e-3 S4 1000 geantinos away from the disk 0 hits: no error, the 95 % limit 1 - 0.05^(1/1000)

The driver's own guarantees (seeds, the order of the merge, extension, prefixes and partial runs, retries, the 128-bit sums, the estimators and their printing) are checked bit for bit with a stand-in program in tests/test_particles_driver.py, including S3 at the level of the estimator (1000 experiments drawn by numpy) and S4 (0 of 10 and of 1e4).

docs.title: The demonstration: a solved solenoid and a tracker
docs.text:
A solenoid (radius 0.5 m, length 1 m, winding 0.05 m thick, 2e5 ampere-turns, domain radius 1.5 m) with eight layers of air 2 mm thick at r = 0.10 to 0.38 m, |z| <= 0.4 m, solved by the package (order 2) and exported as a map at tol 1e-4 with a track volume over the tracker; the partition written by hand with the same regions (the demonstration does not use the mesher's export); mu+ at 0.2 GeV/c from the centre along +x (bore field 0.181 T, radius of curvature about 3.7 m).

check reference measured asserted hits in vacuum (seed 1, 1 event) the map's own trajectory (a test-side Runge-Kutta through FieldMap.evaluate) 2.1e-7 m 2e-5 m momentum scale the same circle fit on the trajectory through the exact closed-form field R(map) / R(exact) - 1 = 7.6e-6, against the map-and-solve error along the path 7.3e-5 2 x 7.3e-5 + 2e-5 circle fit with the path-averaged field 1.0018 2 % (a model) resolution, 1e4 smearings by 50 um exact least squares; Gluckstern (large-N form; the equal-spacing form for 8 layers gives 1.765 %) (1.769 +- 0.013) % against 1.771 % and 1.808 % 2.8 %; 5 % scattering term in air (4000 events, seed 3): the Gaussian core (central 98 %) of the fitted curvature PDG 2024 eq. 35.63 with Highland's logarithm (a formula for many planes; eight here: approximate) (2.365 +- 0.044) % against 2.669 % (-11 %) (the standard deviation, with single-scattering tails, is 3.049 %) 30 %

The 3D iron dipole of the demonstration skips: its test calls particles.transport without solids=, which this version does not serve (capabilities()["partition_export"] is false), although the mesher exports 3D partitions (Design.export_gdml).

docs.title: Test status
docs.text:
Every assertion of the three files passes on the program and the driver of this version (the 3D dipole and, where the application is absent, X1 skip).

X1 (the solids list read back from the exported GDML file by a standalone Geant4 application, axmp-x1, with a Geant4 built with GDML and Xerces-C 3.3.0) applies the same exit and hit rules as the program (interfaces are not exits; a step after a zero-length step records no hit). Against the transport as it was during the development of this version, with the interface rule in place, its three tests passed: volumes and materials bitwise equal, 1e4 geantino crossings and their first random numbers bitwise equal, per-region mean deposits of 2000 electrons of 200 MeV in 0.3 T within 4 sigma (and per-event deposits bitwise equal). The comparison has not been run again against the program of this release, which added the handling of stuck tracks, the per-writer temporary directories and the checks of the gun afterwards.

docs.title: What is not validated
docs.text:
• No comparison with measured data, and no estimate of the physics-list dependence (the three lists run; their differences are not quantified).
  • The convergence evidence of the design note's rule 3 (results with the production cut, the step and the map tolerance halved) is missing; it is left to the next milestone.
  • X1 runs only where its application and a Geant4 built with GDML exist; its tests skip elsewhere.
  • The energy balance of an event (deposits plus escaping energy against the primary's) is not checked: decays and hadronic interactions change the rest-mass energy, which the per-event arrays do not account for.
  • The 3D dipole of the demonstration, and the transport through 3D (tessellated) solids lists in general (they are built and checked by --geometry only).
  • Field maps of 3D solves through the transport (kind-3 maps are checked with analytic fields only).
